### `tools/server/verify_routing_tables.js` — 294 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"THE ROUTING-TABLE GATE."* Its header states the class it owns and why a SECOND gate was needed: *"A navigation table maps a UI id to the NAME of the function that opens it (`WD_ROUTES`, the constellation hub's `panelMap`, …). The openers are invoked through a `typeof window[name] === 'function'` guard, so a name nothing publishes does not throw: the guard is false, the dispatcher returns, and the button is DEAD with no error surface — the exact way `panelMap.governance: 'openGovernance'` (the real publisher is `openGovernancePanel`) silently did nothing. `verify_ui_handlers.js` cannot see this class: it resolves names appearing in MARKUP (`onclick="x()"`). These names appear in a JS TABLE, which no onclick scan reads. **Two input classes, two gates, no duplicated logic.**"*
- **OWNS:** `WD_FILE` (the ONE owner of the routing table), `OPENER_REF_RE` (the `key: 'openX'` shape), `strip`, `walk`, `openerReferences`, the publisher index (`JS_PUBLISH_RE`, `ASSIGN_WINDOW_RE`, `GO_PUBLISH_RE`, `OBJECT_KEY_RE`), `braceBlock`, **`literalBlock`**, `tableBody`, `literalPairs`, `declaredFeatureTabs`, `selftest`, `main`.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** the CLI — `node tools/server/verify_routing_tables.js [--json|--selftest]`; `npm run verify:routes`.
- **CALLS OUT:** nothing network; it walks `Public/**.js` and reads root `*.go` files for the bridge index.
- **DOM/HOST:** none — fully static.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** **none material — the model for a second gate on a second input class.** Named evidence: (1) **`literalBlock` EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIRST VERSION WAS WRONG, AND THE FIX IS DOCUMENTED** — *"Body of the next OBJECT or ARRAY literal at/after `from`, whichever opens first. `WD_ROUTES` is an object but `WD_CATEGORIES` is an ARRAY — matching only braces against the array returned the FIRST CATEGORY's body (9 features instead of 67) and every other feature then looked like an orphan route. **The delimiter is taken from the source, never assumed.**"* — the same self-caught parser bug family session (d) recorded for its own three gates. (2) **THREE PARSE SELF-CHECKS, EACH NAMED WITH ITS CONSEQUENCE** — `if (routes.size === 0) findings.push("WD_ROUTES did not parse into any entry — the table or its name moved; **without this the gate would pass by measuring nothing**.")`, the same for `WD_CATEGORIES` and for `refs.length === 0`. (3) **A REAL NEGATIVE CONTROL** — `selftest()` strips a synthetic `panelMap` with `a: 'openReal'`, `b: 'openMissing'`, `c: null` and requires `found.length === 2 && dead.length === 1 && dead[0] === 'openMissing'` — proving both that a `null` value is skipped (the deliberate "no route") and that an unpublished name is reported. (4) **THE PUBLISHER INDEX COVERS FOUR IDIOMS** — `window.X =`, `window['X'] =`, `globalThis.X =`, the **`Object.assign(window, {…})`** table (via `braceBlock` + `OBJECT_KEY_RE`), and the **Go/WASM bridge `js.Global().Set("X"`** read from root `*.go` — so a bridge-published opener counts, which is how `StartMatch`/`AutoBuildDeck`/`RemoveFromDeck` are real. (5) **TWO INDEPENDENT FINDING CLASSES** — `DEAD ROUTER NAMES` (*"the guard is false, so the control does NOTHING"*) and `ORPHAN ROUTES` (*"routed but not declared as a feature, so nothing can reach them"*) — each with its consequence stated. (6) **It reports the derived taxonomy** — `features routing out / embedding: N / M` — plus `--json` with the full routed/embedding/dead/orphan lists and `failures`. (7) **`process.exitCode = failures ? 1 : 0`** — fails closed. (8) The `strip` scanner is the **same hand-written comment-remover that keeps literals** as `verify_duplicate_modules.js`, reused rather than re-implemented.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the routing-table name class) — **the model for a second gate**: a documented self-caught parser fix, three parse self-checks each naming what a silent pass would mean, a real negative control, four publisher idioms including the Go bridge, two finding classes with their consequences stated, and a fail-closed exit.


### `tools/server/verify_portfolio_associations.js` — 299 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"audit the PORTFOLIO ASSOCIATIONS contract"* — and its header states the gap it closes: *"The Portfolio is the read-only ANALYTICS surface for a wallet. `verify_entry_probe` proves every screen renders WITHOUT a wallet; it cannot prove the wallet-scoped association screens (companions, rivalry, clubs & alliances, bonded assets, faith, custody, obligations) actually resolve their endpoints and report real state. Those screens short-circuit to a connect note when no wallet is present, so a broken URL would go unnoticed. This probe connects a SYNTHETIC wallet, patches `window.fetch` to record every `/api/` request with its HTTP status, opens the Portfolio, walks every category and screen, and reports: per-category render evidence (tables / key-value rows / explicit notes, chars) · the recorded request log (status codes) for the association endpoints · console / page errors. A screen that renders, an endpoint that answers 200, and no errors = pass."*
- **OWNS:** **`SYNTHETIC_WALLET`** (a 71-char structurally-valid AVM address the server has no record for), `resolveChrome`, `httpGet`, `waitFor`, the `CDP` class, the single page-side evaluation, and the report.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** the CLI (`--url`); `npm run verify:portfolio`.
- **CALLS OUT:** the two CDP discovery endpoints, and **`GET /api/player/associations?wallet=`** probed FIRST, plus every `/api/` route the sweep's screens touch (logged).
- **DOM/HOST:** spawns headless Chrome with a **dedicated port (9447)** and its own temp profile (`vbt-assoc-`), polls for readiness, walks `.pp-cat` / the sub-screen list, and reports per-category.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** **none material — the strongest browser-tier gate in the tree.** Named evidence: (1) **IT POLLS FOR READINESS INSTEAD OF SLEEPING** — *"Poll for readiness: the app boots through wasm_exec, so a fixed wait is flaky under load. Wait until the Portfolio entry point exists."* — up to 50 × 500 ms on `typeof window.openPortfolio === 'function'`, then **throws if it never appears** (`window.openPortfolio never became available`). This is the fix the entry probe later needed too. (2) **ONE EVALUATION FOR THE WHOLE SWEEP, WITH THE REASON STATED** — *"ONE evaluation: patch → connect wallet → open Portfolio → sweep. Splitting these across Runtime.evaluate calls loses the closure scope (and the fetch log), which silently produced an empty report."* — a real defect the author hit and named. (3) **THE CONTRACT PROBE IS FIRST, WITH THE RATE-LIMIT RULE STATED** — *"Probed FIRST, while the wallet-default rate-limit bucket is fresh. A 429 is retried once (exactly the rule the Portfolio itself applies); if it is STILL refused the read is reported as 'could not be read' rather than as a contract violation — there is no body to assert against."* — and the verdict ladder is explicit: `OK` / **`RATE-LIMITED (accepted)`** / `FAIL`. **A refused read is neither a pass nor a violation**, the honest classification `Problems.md §26 E` established. (4) **IT ASSERTS THREE BINDING CONTRACTS ON THE EXPORT** — HTTP 200, **null-free** (*"a null map/slice would let a reader confuse 'not exported' with 'empty'"*), and **float-free** (*"Architecture Ledger: integer micro-units only"*), the latter via a recursive walk recording the PATH of any non-integer number (`contract.floats = contract.floats.slice(0, 8)`). (5) **EVERY screen is judged on RENDERED evidence** — `chars`, `blocks`, `notes` — with `row.chars === 0 || row.failed || row.loading` collecting the bad ones, so a loading spinner and a silent empty screen are both caught. (6) **THE ENDPOINT LOG IS DEDUPED AND SORTED**, and **5xx/network-error are separated from 4xx** (`(e[1] >= 500 || e[1] === 0)`) — a 404 is correctly NOT a failure here, because a wallet-scoped route may legitimately answer not-found. (7) **The exit code requires ALL FOUR** — `bad.length || errored.length || errors.length || !contractOk`. (8) **A skip is a bare exit 0** (`'[ASSOC] No browser found — skipped.'`) — the ONE weakness it shares with `ui_test_harness.js`.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the Portfolio associations contract) — **the standard for a wallet-scoped browser gate**: it polls readiness, runs the sweep in ONE evaluation because splitting it lost the log, probes the export FIRST on a fresh rate-limit bucket, treats a refused read as unread rather than as a verdict, and asserts the three binding contracts (200, null-free, float-free) with the path of any offender.

### ⚠️ LEDGER NOTE — the `tools\` JS rows, counted rather than inferred
The `tools\` JS rows mapped by this sweep number **NINE**, not the seven an earlier note in this file stated: `ui_test_harness.js` · `verify_overlay_visibility.js` · `verify_duplicate_modules.js` · `verify_routing_tables.js` · `verify_portfolio_associations.js` · `flow_debug.js` · `flow_verify.js` · `archscan/render.js` · `archscan/archlib.js`. The earlier figure was taken from a `--`-padded display list rather than counted; **this note supersedes it**, and all nine are mapped.


### `Public/collective-intelligence.js` — 307 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"Collective NPC Intelligence - Narrative Logic. Analyzes player playstyle tendencies and generates contextual taunts."*
- **OWNS:** **`collectiveIntelligence`** — an ESM export with `personalities` (4 NPC personalities: **The Architect**, **Jackpot Jessica**, **The Enforcer**, **The Oracle**) and **`generatePlaystyleTaunt(npcName, playstyle)`** — and the whole taunt corpus (4 personalities × 4 tendency axes × 2-4 moods, ~180 hand-written taunt strings).
- **ENTRY POINTS:** `export const collectiveIntelligence` — **no `window.` binding**; consumed by `economy.js` and `game.js`.
- **CALLS OUT:** **NOTHING** — no fetch, no `/api/` string. It READS a playstyle object the caller supplies.
- **DOM/HOST:** none — pure string generation.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THIS IS THE FILE SESSION (d) FOUND DUPLICATED, AND IT IS THE IMPLEMENTATION THE ALIAS FORWARDS TO.** Session (d) measured that `Public/js/collective-intelligence.js` was a **SECOND, EMPTY registry** (729 B, `personalities: {}`, no `generatePlaystyleTaunt`) beside this real one, that **nothing imported it**, and that it was *"a trap waiting for the first in-directory import."* The fix made the small copy a **documented re-export ALIAS** and pointed `economy.js`/`game.js` at it in-directory. **This file's 307 lines and ~180 taunts are exactly what the empty decoy was pretending to be.** (2) **`Math.random()` PICKS THE TAUNT** — `const baseTaunt = tendencies[Math.floor(Math.random() * tendencies.length)]` with the comment *"Pick a random taunt from the collected possibilities"*. Interpolated into a served narrative string, this is **non-deterministic NPC output** — the class `game_modes.js`'s casino dice and `achievement_service.go`'s random trophy unlock also belong to, though at lower stakes. Stated precisely: the determinism mandate's enumerated prohibitions are balances/transfers/taxes/rewards/debts/interest/fees/royalties/career-combat XP/ledger counters — **a taunt is not in that list**, so this is a determinism smell rather than a ledger violation: the honest reading is "the NPC says something different on every call with identical inputs". (3) **A MEASURED CROSS-FILE SCALE MISMATCH.** `playstyle` is a server field name, and its sub-fields are read with **three naming conventions** — `playstyle.aggressiveness`/`riskTolerance` in **camelCase**, `preferred_rules`/`preferred_card_moods` in **snake_case**, with threshold keys `'Plus'`/`'Same'` and moods in **PascalCase** (`Volatile`/`Serene`/`Spirited`/`Grounded`). More importantly the thresholds compare against **0..1 floats** (`> 0.75`, `< 0.25`, `> 0.8`, `< 0.2`, `> 1.5`) while the Go sweep recorded `handlePlayerAssociations` converting engine playstyle ratios into **integer parts-per-million** at the HTTP boundary — so **every comparison is against the wrong scale and the engine likely returns `null` for every real player** (`tendencies.length === 0`). (4) **`personalities[npcName]` IS AN EXACT-KEY LOOKUP WITH A SILENT DEFAULT** — *"Default to 'The Architect' if name not found or generic"* — so a misspelled NPC name gets the Architect's voice rather than a report. (5) The docstring's contract (*"A taunt string or null if no significant behavior is found"*) is honoured by the code. (6) **The corpus is genuinely authored** — four distinct voices (flamboyant / cryptic / intimidating / analytical), each with 2-4 variants per axis — which is precisely why its duplication as an EMPTY file mattered.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the NPC taunt corpus) — a real, hand-authored four-personality narrative engine whose one measured defect is a **scale mismatch against the served parts-per-million playstyle fields** (making its thresholds unreachable for a real player), plus a `Math.random()` pick and three naming conventions in one payload contract.


### `Public/js/deck.js` — 312 lines
- **PURPOSE:** the Deck Manager — inventory → active deck drag/drop, the four reputation-gated deck slots, the avatar grid with a crop/zoom frame, and the blockchain inventory refresh. No header block; one of the oldest modules (it imports from `config`, `network`, `ui`, `wallet`, `utils` and `game`).
- **OWNS:** `userNFTs`, `currentAvatarUrl`, **`cropState`** (`{x, y, zoom}`), `isCropInitialized`, plus four explicit setters (`setUserNFTs`, `setCurrentAvatarUrl`, `setCropState`, `setIsCropInitialized`).
- **ENTRY POINTS:** named ESM exports — `openDeckManager`, `closeDeckManager`, `renderDeckManager`, `renderAvatarGrid`, `applyAvatarFilters`, `selectAvatar`, `setupCropEvents`, `refreshInventory` — plus the four setters and the state exports; **`window.renderDeckManager` is bound at the tail** with the fix recorded: *"The deck manager's Auto-Build button in index.html calls `renderDeckManager()` bare, and an inline handler resolves that name on `window` — the function is a module export, so the call threw after AutoBuildDeck had already run and the manager never refreshed with the new deck."*
- **CALLS OUT:** **`GET /api/card-details?wallet=`** (a bare `fetch`, not the shared helper) and the WS `update_rating` / `register_avatar` sends; engine globals `window.GetGameState`, `window.syncUI`, `window.selectCard`, `window.SelectDeck`, `window.RemoveFromDeck`, `window.SetAvatar`, `window.ImportARC72Card`, `calculateDeckRating`.
- **DOM/HOST:** `#deck-manager-overlay` (legacy `.hidden` contract — the opener calls `hideAllOverlays()` then `classList.remove('hidden')`), `#inventory-grid`, `#deck-drop-zone`, `#deck-selector-bar`, `#total-atk`, `#total-def`, `#avatar-grid`, `#avatar-search`, `#avatar-sort`, `#avatar-preview-section`, `#crop-image`, `#crop-frame`, `#zoom-slider`, `#zoom-val`, `#confirm-avatar-btn`, `#gloat-message-input`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **A FOUR-SLOT REPUTATION LADDER IS CLIENT-DECLARED** — `const thresholds = [0, 250, 600, 1000]` with `state.reputation < thresholds[i]` gating each slot and the label `🔒 N REP`. The gate reads engine state (good) but the **four thresholds are hard-coded here** — another invented ladder beside `leaderboard.js`'s donation tiers and `loan_terms.js`'s credit score. (2) **`state.reputation` IS READ WITHOUT THE GUARD THE SAME FUNCTION APPLIES TWO LINES EARLIER** — `if (!state || !state.inventory || !state.deck) return;` protects the pools, then the slot loop dereferences `state.reputation` unguarded. (3) **`card.power[0..3]` IS INDEXED UNGUARDED IN THE DECK-STACK TOTALS** — `totalAtk += (card.power[0] + card.power[1])` — so a malformed card throws mid-render, while `card?.name` is optional-chained two lines away, showing the author knew the shape was uncertain. (4) **THE CROP FRAME'S MOUSE LISTENERS ARE ADDED TO `window` AND NEVER REMOVED** — `window.addEventListener('mousemove', …)` / `('mouseup', …)` inside `setupCropEvents`, guarded by `isCropInitialized` so they attach once **for the page's lifetime** — and the drag has **no touch/pointer handling**, while the app's menu wheel uses pointer capture for exactly that reason. (5) **`img.onload` SETS THE ZOOM SLIDER'S `min`/`max` FROM THE IMAGE'S NATURAL SIZE** and `zoomVal` shows `"1.0x"` before any input — a real, working crop UI whose geometry is float, presentation only. (6) **`localStorage.setItem("vbabes_gloat_msg", gloat)` STORES A PLAYER-WRITTEN TAUNT VERBATIM** and `SetAvatar(url, gloat, "", state.favorite_card_id || 0)` passes it to the engine — avatar and gloat are genuine server-bound state (via `SetAvatar` and the `register_avatar` WS message), so the path is real. (7) **`refreshInventory` CALLS `/api/card-details?wallet=` THEN `ImportARC72Card(card.id, "Voi Mainnet")` PER CARD** — *"Standards resolved by backend MetadataDispatcher"* — with the network hard-coded to Voi, consistent with Voi-as-base-chain. (8) `applyAvatarFilters` calls `.toLowerCase()` on `search` **without a guard** (`?.value.toLowerCase()` guards the element, not the result). (9) **Failure is honest** — the catch logs `[DECK] Sync Failed:` and leaves the shimmer, a stuck state rather than a false statement.
- **VERDICT:** ambiguous → the real Deck Manager with a real crop UI and a real card sync, carrying a client-declared four-slot reputation ladder, two unguarded `power[]` index reads, page-lifetime mouse listeners with no pointer support, and one in-place record of a dead-name fix.

### `tools/server/verify_module_reachability.js` — 374 lines
- **PURPOSE:** ***"verify_module_reachability.js — THE COMPOSITION-GRAPH GATE."*** Its header states the whole reason for existing: *"The Single-Entry Mandate makes `Public/index.html` a pure shell and `Public/app.js` the ONE composition root: every first-party module must be REACHABLE from it. A module nothing imports cannot render, cannot publish a global and cannot be reached by any route — it is dead code with a file size. Nothing measured that, and the metric that looked like it did (archscan's `isReferenced`) answers a different question: 'is this path mentioned anywhere?', which a mention INSIDE another unloaded module satisfies. **Referenced is not reachable**, and the gap between them is where built-and-forgotten modules live."*
- **OWNS:** the `BASELINE` holding pen, `ROOTS`, `SKIP_DIR`/`SKIP_FILES`, `strip()`, `walk()`, `rootJsFiles()`, `htmlPages()`, `specifiersOf()`, `resolveSpec()`, `selftest()`, `main()`.
- **EDGES MEASURED (six forms, each named):** ESM `import … from`, `export … from`, `export * from`, dynamic `import('…')` with a LITERAL specifier, side-effect `import '…'`, and **classic script injection** (`<script src="…">` / `el.src = '…js'`).
- **FAILURE CRITERIA (exit 1):** (1) a specifier resolving to NO file (*"the module silently never evaluates"*); (2) an unreachable module NOT baselined; (3) **a baselined module that BECAME reachable** — *"a stale entry means the baseline is legitimising rot instead of recording it"*; plus the CANARY.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS / MERITS:** **this is the model gate, and its merits are measured rather than asserted.** (1) **IT NAMES THE FALSE METRIC IT REPLACES AND WHY THAT METRIC WAS BELIEVABLE** — `archscan`'s `isReferenced` is quoted, its question stated, and the exact way a mention inside an unloaded module satisfies it. A gate that explains the wrong answer it supersedes is maintenance-resistant. (2) **THE STALE-ENTRY RULE IS THE DESIGN CHOICE WORTH COPYING** — most baselines fail only on a NEW finding; this one fails on a RESOLVED one, so the pen must SHRINK as verdicts land. (3) **`selftest()` CARRIES THE PARSER BUGS THE GATE ACTUALLY HAD, DOCUMENTED IN PLACE** — *"Negative control. These are the exact parser facts that were WRONG on the first run of this gate, each of which silently reported live modules as unreachable: a static `import { X } from '…'` must be seen (only side-effect/dynamic imports carry no `from`), a commented-out import must NOT be seen, and a classic `el.src = 'js/x.js'` must resolve against the DOCUMENT."* It writes **real temp files** into `os.tmpdir()`, asserts four shapes, and exits 1 on any failure — a control that can fail, naming its own history. (4) **`strip()` EXPLAINS ITS OWN CONTRACT** — *"A commented-out import is not an edge, and a URL inside a string is not code. Removed text becomes spaces so offsets stay meaningful."* — and it **keeps literal TEXT** (`// keep the literal TEXT (specifiers live inside)`) while blanking HTML comments, `//`, `/* */`, escapes and all three quote styles. (5) **THE ASSET-VS-MODULE DISTINCTION IS STATED** — *"An asset URL that matches no file in this repo is not a first-party module; only a MODULE specifier that resolves nowhere is a genuine broken import."* — with `pageRelative` controlling both the base and whether an unresolved path becomes `{external:true}` or `{missing:…}`. (6) **THE CANARY IS A COUNT, NOT A CHECK** — `inventory.size < 100` yields *"the module walk found only N first-party file(s) — check the SKIP rules; **the gate is measuring nothing**"*; without it a walk that silently returned nothing would make every module look reachable. (7) **`--json` SERVES THE CLOSURE ITSELF, WITH THE REASON** — *"The closure itself, so a downstream measurement can ask 'is this module COMPOSED?' without re-deriving the graph (**one owner per question**)."* — the interface that let session (f) re-measure the twelve unowned endpoints without a second graph. (8) **THE BASELINE'S OWN HISTORY IS THE HOLDING-PEN RECORD** — the five retired shells with each fact marked as a measurement, and `theme_engine.js`'s WIRE verdict with its inert-contract reasoning — so the pen's emptiness is auditable rather than merely empty. **Honest limits stated by the file:** it reads STATIC facts only (a specifier built by concatenation is invisible); `resolveSpec` tries bare, `.js` and `/index.js` and nothing else; `architecture.html` is skipped as a generated report; `SKIP_DIR` excludes vendor/node_modules/prototypes/Assets/Generated/devdata/.git.
- **VERDICT:** owner — **the composition-graph gate and the strongest of the tooling family**: it names the false metric it replaces, fails on a STALE entry as well as a new one, carries a real negative control documenting the parser bugs it actually had, guards itself with a canary, and serves its closure so no second graph is ever derived.

- **DOM/HOST:** requires `#life-assets-overlay`; hosts `.la-tab`, `.la-panel`, `#la-pets-grid`, `#la-veh-grid`, `#la-veh-name`, `#la-veh-kind`, `#la-veh-classes`, `#la-veh-spawn`, `#la-wc-*`, `#la-event-*`, `#la-status`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **A DUPLICATED `addEventListener` ON THE VEHICLE BUY BUTTON, MEASURED** — `init()` registers it **TWICE**: `document.getElementById('la-veh-spawn').addEventListener('click', onSpawnVeh);` appears on two consecutive lines. `onSpawnVeh` therefore runs **twice per click**, sending **two `POST /api/vehicles/spawn` requests** — and because `SpawnVehicle` is now a **purchase** (the class table owns the price, per the Go sweep), a double-registered listener is a **double charge from a single click**. There is no `busy` lock in this file to make the second call harmless. (2) **THE PET TAB IS A HAND-OFF, NOT A DUPLICATE — WITH THE COMMENT SAYING SO** — *"NOTE: no pet-purchase listener here — the Kennel owns companion acquisition/progression."* — while the tab renders *"Companion purchase, breeding and grooming are owned by the **Companion Kennel** … This panel no longer duplicates those controls."* This is the **resolved form** of the duplication the (g) pass recorded (the Kennel owns purchase/breeding/grooming). (3) **THE §25.6.1 LADDER IS FULLY SERVED-DRIVEN** — the part table, `part_max_level` and `base_cost_micro` are read from `/api/vehicles` with the comment *"the part table is server-owned — the client never re-declares it"*; the class dropdown is built from the served `spawn_fees` (*"the server decides each class's price + Level gate"*); and `onSpawnVeh` **deliberately omits `min_level`**: *"No min_level is sent: the class owns the Level gate AND the price (§25.6.1)."* — matching the server contract exactly. (4) **THE DOUBLE-PREFIX DEFECT IS RECORDED IN PLACE WITH ITS CONSEQUENCE** — `refresh()`'s comment: *"Paths are relative to API_BASE (which already ends in /api). The previous revision passed '/api/pets' into a helper that prepends '/api', so every read 404'd and the whole panel reported 'Load failed' — the Garage could never populate."* (5) **A REFUSED READ IS REPORTED, NEVER RENDERED AS EMPTY** — `api('/pets' + w).catch(e => ({ __err: … }))` per call, then *"A refused read is reported as refused — never rendered as 'you own nothing'."* and `setStatus('Some reads were refused — ' + refused.join('; '))`: per-call fault tolerance, the shape the Portfolio established. (6) **`walletQS()` EXISTS BECAUSE THE SERVER RESOLVES THE OWNER FROM THE REQUEST** — *"Every write route here resolves the wallet from the request (header or query), so the panel MUST send one — without it the server can only answer 'owner required'."* (7) **`onResolveEvent` RENDERS CREDITS BY FLOAT DIVISION INTO UNESCAPED `innerHTML`** — `${(m / 1000000).toFixed(4)} $VBV` and `${w.slice(0, 8)}…` are interpolated with no `esc()`, although `w` is a server wallet (safe alphabet) and `m` a number; the file has `esc()` and uses it elsewhere (`value="${esc(o.entityId)}"`). (8) **`onResolveEvent` SENDS NO WALLET** — unlike every other write here, `POST /api/entity-event/resolve` carries `{event_id, outcomes}` with **no `walletQS()`**. (9) **`window._laView3D` WAITS A HARD-CODED 350 ms** before warping the 3D engine — a guessed window, in contrast to `world3d.js`'s own `mount()`-if-needed `warpToRegion`.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the Garage / World Content / Entity Events tabs) — a served-price progression panel of the same quality as the Kennel, whose one measured defect is a **duplicated click listener on the vehicle purchase button** (a double charge on a now-priced door), plus an unescaped credit read-out, a wallet-less event-resolve call, and a guessed 350 ms race window.

- **DOM/HOST:** none — a pure preference store.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THE SNEAKY-IST D: 8 `syncToWasm()` CALL SITES AGAINST 10 WRITERS.** `toggleStar`, `unstar`, `reorderStarred`, `setMenuLayout`, `setMainMenu`, `setButtonOverride`, `removeButtonOverride`, `setDefaultShape`, `setDefaultSize`, `setGridType`, `importPrefs` and `resetAll` all propagate to the bridge — **`bindAsset` calls `save(); notify();` and STOPS** — so **a bound asset is never propagated to the engine menu state**, an inconsistency *inside the field it writes* (`starred.assetId`, which IS mirrored) rather than only across fields. `setPlaceholder` omits it too: defensible for placeholders, but the asymmetry with `boundAssets` is stated nowhere. (2) **A PERSISTED SHAPE WITH NO PER-KEY MIGRATION — the recurring class, and `gridSpin` is the proof it already bit.** `load()` does `Object.assign({}, DEFAULTS, JSON.parse(raw))` and then guards only the TOP-LEVEL keys (`starred`, `boundAssets`, `layout`, `mainMenu`, `menuLayout`) — so a **new `menuLayout` key is ABSENT on every existing user's state** because the stored object replaces `DEFAULTS.menuLayout` wholesale. That is exactly what `gridSpin` needed, and the mitigation ended up as a fallback at each reader instead of a migration. `importPrefs` reproduces the hole: `Object.assign({}, DEFAULTS, data)` with no nested validation, and it replaces `_state` **without the `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))` deep copy** the other paths use, so an imported object's nested references are adopted live. (3) **`DEFAULTS` NEVER DECLARES `placeholders`, YET FIVE GUARDS DEFEND IT** — `if (!s.placeholders) s.placeholders = {};` in `setPlaceholder` and `load().placeholders?.[tabId] || null` / `load().placeholders || {}` in the two getters — so the store is coherent **by accident rather than by declaration**, which is why the `placeholders` path reads differently from the DECLARED `boundAssets` path. (4) **`syncFromWasm`'S EMPTY-GUARD IS DOCUMENTED WITH THE BUG IT FIXED** — *"Only adopt WASM favorites when WASM actually has curated items. An empty WASM menu-state must never wipe the user's localStorage favorites (this caused the Favorites grid to flicker 1 -> 0 -> 1)."* — a real flicker defect recorded at the site of its fix. (5) **`syncFromWasm` ENDS WITH AN UNCONDITIONAL `save()`** — the mirror writes `localStorage` on every read-back even when it changed nothing, so a WASM→local round trip is a write. (6) **`notify()` SWALLOWS LISTENER EXCEPTIONS WITH NO REPORT** — `try { fn(_state); } catch (e) {}` — the one place in this file where a failure is neither logged nor surfaced, so a listener that always throws is silently dead. (7) **`exportPrefs`/`importPrefs` ARE A COMPLETE, HONEST ROUND TRIP** (pretty-printed JSON out; try/parse in; `true`/`false` returned; `console.error` on failure) — the best-behaved pair in the file. (8) **`reorderStarred` BOUNDS-CHECKS BOTH INDICES** and returns silently on an out-of-range one: correct, but the caller gets no signal.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of user preference persistence) — a clean, well-documented store whose two real defects are structural: **a persisted shape with no per-key migration** (which the `gridSpin` addition already required and did not get) and **`bindAsset` omitting the `syncToWasm()` every sibling writer performs**.

- **CALLS OUT:** **one live endpoint family only: `/api/compliance/summary`, `/api/compliance/records`, `POST /api/compliance/escalate|resolve`** (the `initCompliance` block). **The other thirteen make NO request at all.**
- **DOM/HOST:** requires `#wd-launches`, `#wd-ads`, `#wd-vehicles`, `#wd-stats`, `#wd-worldcontent`, `#wd-gamingos`, `#wd-localmodel`, `#wd-governor`, `#wd-leaderboard`, `#wd-compliance`, `#wd-maintenance`, `#wd-systemmsg`, `#wd-orphan`, `#wd-regions`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THIRTEEN OF FOURTEEN PANELS ARE STATIC FIXTURES PRESENTED AS ENGINE DATA — the fabricated-UI class at scale.** Each renders a named entity with a status that was never read: **`Season 2 Update`/`Active`** (Launchpad) · **`Arena Promo`/`Running`** (Ads) · **`Speedster`/`Idle`** (Vehicles) · **`Castle`/`Active`** (World Content) · **`Economy`/`Active`** (Gaming OS) · **`0` Power Level / `0` Effective / `0` Stat Sum** (Stats) · **`Base`/`0 instances`/`GPU`** (Local LLM) · **`0` Voting Power / `None` Delegated** (Governor) · **`#1 Player 0`** (Leaderboard) · **`System Active`** (Maintenance) · **`Welcome to the Arena`/`Now`** (System Msg). (2) **THREE OF THEM ASSERT STATE RATHER THAN DECORATE** — the **Maintenance** panel's `System Active` claims a system status it never reads; the **Governor** panel presents `0 Voting Power / None Delegated` as *the player's* figures having read nothing; the **Leaderboard** panel renders a ranking `#1 Player 0` with no source. (3) **`initRegions` INVENTS A REGION LITERALLY NAMED `Governor`** — `<span class="region-name">Governor</span><span class="region-status">Neutral</span>` — the same sample-data defect recorded for `territory_map.js`. (4) **SIX PANELS DUPLICATE FEATURES THAT HAVE A REAL ROUTED OWNER** — `initVehicles` (`WD_ROUTES.vehicles → openLifeAssets`), `initWorldContent` (the Garage's World Content tab), `initStatsOverlay` (`openStatOverlay`), `initLeaderboard` (`openLeaderboardRegion`), `initGovernor` (the governance leaf) and `initOrphans` (`orphan_cleaner.js`, which `WD_ROUTES.orphan` routes to) each render a static stand-in for a feature that is fully implemented elsewhere and is reached by ROUTING OUT rather than embedding. (5) **`initOrphans`' ADOPT/RECLAIM BUTTONS HAVE NO HANDLER AT ALL** — two `vbt-btn` controls with **no `onclick` and no listener**, while `extended_dashboard.js` owns `edOrphanAdopt`/`edOrphanReclaim` for the same `/api/orphan/*` routes: dead controls on a duplicated panel. (6) **`initCompliance` IS THE EXCEPTION AND IS FULLY REPAIRED — the session (f) fix is recorded in place:** *"This leaf used to be FABRICATED: it rendered a hard-coded 'KYC / Clear' row and made no request at all, so a player saw a compliance record the engine had never produced. It now reads the engine's REAL records and exposes the two lifecycle controls that had no owner anywhere in the client — POST /api/compliance/escalate and POST /api/compliance/resolve … The summary above them is the server's own counts."* It has its own prefix-safe `complianceApi`, its own `complianceEsc`, **per-call fault tolerance with a `problems[]` list**, a summary rendered from **whatever keys the server sent** (`Object.entries(summary)`), a severity class taken from the served value, `addEventListener` for both verbs, and **a refusal rendered as `"Escalate refused: " + message`**. That block is the standard the other thirteen need.
- **VERDICT:** **ambiguous → predominantly a duplication + fabrication surface.** Thirteen of fourteen panels are static fixtures presented as engine data (three of them asserting state), six duplicate features that have a real routed owner, and two controls have no handler — while the fourteenth (`initCompliance`) shows exactly what the repaired form looks like. The honest verdict is **retire the thirteen, keep `initCompliance`** (or move it under a real owner), because every capability they gesture at is owned elsewhere.


### `Public/js/wallet.js` — 451 lines
- **PURPOSE:** no header block — the wallet rail: WalletConnect init + session restore, the nonce-gated reward payout, the payout-address setting, and the linked-wallet proof.
- **OWNS:** `userAddress`, `isVerified`, `linkedWallets`, `payoutAddress`, `walletProvider`, `signClient`, `wcModal`, plus five setters (`setWalletProvider`, `setPayoutAddress`, `setUserAddress`, `setIsVerified`, `setLinkedWallets`) which are the only writers every importing module uses.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** ESM exports (`initWalletConnect`, `openPayoutSettings`, `savePayoutAddress`, `updatePayoutUI`, `processRewardPayout`, `handleWalletAction`, `closeWalletSelector`, `submitLinkWallet`, …) + **`window.processRewardPayout`** (called by the engine) + **`window.onLinkWalletResponse`** (the WS consumer).
- **CALLS OUT:** **`POST /api/bridge/onboard`** `{wallet}` · **`POST /api/reward`** (the nonce-gated payout) · WS `nonce_request` and `link_wallet_request` · `setNonceResolver` from `network.js`.
- **DOM/HOST:** legacy `.hidden` contract — `#payout-settings-overlay`, `#wallet-selector-overlay`, `#link-wallet-overlay`; `#payout-address-input`, `#payout-address-display`, `#linked-address-input`, `#linked-chain-select`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THE SESSION-RESTORE IS DEFENSIVE AND ITS REASONING IS IN PLACE** — *"Restore existing session (defensive: iterate namespaces, validate chain)."* — it walks session → namespace → account, **parses the CAIP-2 chain id out of the account string** (`parts[0] + ':' + parts[1]`), validates against `[CONFIG.VOI_CHAIN_ID, CONFIG.ALGO_CHAIN_ID]`, and only then adopts `parts[2]`. This is the 2026-09-13 (d) hardening replacing a blind `namespaces.algorand.accounts[0]` read. (2) **`submitLinkWallet` FINDS THE CORRECT SESSION FOR THE ADDRESS IT IS PROVING** — *"PILLAR 3: Robust Signature Acquisition. Find the correct WalletConnect session and chainId for the linkedAddress."* — it scans `signClient.session.getAll()`, matches with `a.toLowerCase().includes(linkedAddress.toLowerCase())` (**case-insensitive**, this repository's recurring class handled correctly), derives `targetChainId` from the matched account, and refuses with a stated reason: `` `No active session found for ${linkedAddress}. Please connect that wallet via WalletConnect.` `` (3) **TWO SIGNATURE PROTOCOLS, EXPLICITLY DISTINGUISHED** — `solana_signMessage` (`params: {message, pubkey}`) for `sol`, and **`personal_sign` with `params: [nonce, linkedAddress]`** for EVM (*"Pass raw nonce string"*). **There is NO AVM branch**, matching the Go sweep's measurement that the link handler has no AVM case either — so **a Voi wallet cannot be linked from either side**. (4) **A REAL DEFECT: THE PAYOUT BODY'S AUTHORITY IS CLIENT-ASSERTED.** `payload.claimant = payload.recipient;` then `payload.recipient = payoutAddress || payload.recipient;` — **the client rewrites the recipient to its own stored `payoutAddress` and declares `claimant` itself**. The nonce IS fetched from the server first (a real replay guard), and it is carried as the transaction's **note** with `amount: 0`, `from == to`, `type: 'pay'` — a **zero-amount self-transaction whose note holds the nonce** — so the door's security rests entirely on what the server checks against `signed_tx`. (5) **TWO `String.fromCharCode(...spread)` CALLS WITH NO SIZE BOUND** — the WalletConnect payout branch builds the transaction as `btoa(String.fromCharCode(...algosdk.encodeObj(tx)))` and decodes the response with `atob(response[0]).split("").map(c => c.charCodeAt(0))`; **a spread into `String.fromCharCode` throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` above roughly 65 KB**, and an encoded transaction can approach that. (6) **`savePayoutAddress` VALIDATES BY LENGTH ALONE** — `addr.length === 58` — with no checksum, no base32 alphabet check and no address decode, so any 58-character string is accepted, stored and later used as a payout destination; the Go sweep recorded the server-side `DecodeAddress` errors as **discarded**, so nothing downstream rejects it. (7) **`updatePayoutUI` SLICES BY MAGIC OFFSETS** — `substring(0, 6) + "..." + substring(54)` assumes exactly 58 characters, correct only because (6) enforces the length. (8) **`initWalletConnect` REFUSES A PLACEHOLDER PROJECT ID BY NAME** — `if (!projectId || projectId.toLowerCase().includes('project_id'))` — so the shipped sentinel is detected and reported rather than attempted. (9) **`window.onLinkWalletResponse` IS ONE OF THE NINE WIRED WS CONSUMERS**, defined exactly once here (a second definition would silently win) — it toasts the outcome and removes `#link-wallet-overlay` on success. (10) **`handleWalletAction` READS `window.userAddress`** (a global) while the module's authority is the `userAddress` **binding** it exports: two spellings of one fact, and only one of them is the variable every other module imports.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the wallet rail) — the module holding the session-restore hardening, the two-protocol link proof and the nonce-gated payout; its real defects are a **length-only payout-address validation with no checksum**, a **client-rewritten recipient in the payout body**, and **two unbounded `String.fromCharCode(...spread)` calls** on the WalletConnect branch.

### `Public/js/controller_nav.js` — 480 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"Universal gamepad/keyboard/tilt navigation"* — *"PC: DirectInput/XInput gamepads, keyboard fallback · Console: Xbox, PlayStation, Nintendo (via browser Gamepad API) · Android: Bluetooth gamepads, touch tilt (device orientation) · All: D-pad/stick → grid navigation, face buttons → select/back."* Eight numbered sections: detection, listeners, polling loop, action handler, haptics, console adaptations, public API.
- **OWNS:** `CONTROLLER_TYPES` (7), `STATE` (deadZone 0.3, repeatDelay 200, repeatRate 80, focusIndex), the standard-Gamepad `BTN` map, `BTN_LABELS` per platform, `moveFocus`/`setFocus`/`activateItem`, `hapticFeedback`, `injectConsoleHints`.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** 13-name ESM export (`init`, `STATE`, `CONTROLLER_TYPES`, `BTN_LABELS`, `handleAction`, `setFocus`, `showFocusRing`, `hideFocusRing`, `hapticFeedback`, `injectConsoleHints`, `getConsoleHint`, `getActiveGamepad`, `detectControllerType`) + `enable`/`disable`/`isActive`/`getType`/`getFocusIndex` — **no `window.` binding**, and it **self-inits** on `DOMContentLoaded`.
- **CALLS OUT:** `window.HandleControllerInput`, `window.SetControllerType`, `window.SetControllerFocus` (the WASM bridge) · `window.UserPreferences.getMenuLayout()` · `getControllerNav` imported from `menu_customization.js` (**imported and NEVER USED** — no reference in the file).
- **DOM/HOST:** requires **`#ch-starred-grid`** and navigates `.ch-starred-btn, .preview-btn`; **creates `#controller-hints`** by appending to `grid.parentElement`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THE GRID-TYPE VOCABULARY CONTAINS THE TWO IDS SESSION (e) MEASURED AS NOT EXISTING — `'linear-h'` AND `'linear-v'`.** This file switches on `gridType` for `'grid'`, `'circle'`, **`'linear-h'`/`'arc'`**, **`'linear-v'`/`'triangle'`**, `'cross'`, `'diamond'` and a `default`. The 2026-09-15 (e) pass measured that the *"engine's keys are `linearH`/`linearV`"* while both `menu-constellation.js` and the customization panel were testing `['grid','linear-h','linear-v']`, so those guards never fired. **This is a THIRD consumer carrying the dead spellings**, and it has a `default` branch — so a `linearH` layout silently falls through to the sequential `right/down → +1` rule, meaning **a horizontal layout navigates as a list on a controller**. It is the only one of the three with a fallback, which is why nothing broke visibly. (2) **`STATE.repeatRate` (80 ms) IS NEVER READ** — the poll loop gates on `repeatDelay` (200 ms) and then sets `lastMoveTime = now`, so the intended fast-repeat phase **does not exist**: holding a stick moves at 5 cells/second, not the 12.5 the state implies. A declared constant with no reader. (3) **`handleAction` CALLS `window.HandleControllerInput` AND THEN ALSO MOVES FOCUS ITSELF** — it asks the WASM bridge for a new focus index **and** separately runs `moveFocus(gridType, items, direction)` on `#ch-starred-grid`; the bridge's answer is written into `STATE.focusIndex` and then immediately overwritten by `setFocus`. Two owners for one focus index, with the local one winning — the mirrored-state class the architecture ledger forbids. (4) **POLL GATES `move`/`select`/`back` DIFFERENTLY** — the D-pad/stick path honours `repeatDelay`; **`A` (select) and `B` (back) re-fire on EVERY animation frame while held** (`if (pad.buttons[BTN.A]?.pressed) { handleAction('select'); return; }` with no time check), so holding A activates the focused item ~60 times a second. That is a real double-fire path on any controller "select" that performs an action. (5) **`hapticFeedback` IS EXPORTED AND NEVER CALLED** — the rumble engine (three effect profiles) has **no caller in this file or any other constructor**; only the exported API exposes it. (6) **THE FOCUS INDEX SURVIVES A LAYOUT CHANGE BECAUSE `moveFocus` CLAMPS** (`newIndex = Math.max(0, Math.min(count - 1, newIndex))`) — correct — **but `'cross'` and `'diamond'` ASSIGN A FIXED INDEX PER DIRECTION** (`crossMap[direction] ?? 0`), so pressing "up" in a cross layout jumps to index 1 regardless of where the user is: the cross/diamond shapes are mapped as if the layout were a fixed 4-node pad. (7) **`injectConsoleHints` REBUILDS THE HINT BAR ON EVERY CALL** (it looks the element up and rewrites `innerHTML`), and **`hideFocusRing` never removes it** — so a disconnected controller leaves the hint bar showing the labels of a controller that is gone. (8) **THE DEVICE-ORIENTATION LISTENER IS REGISTERED UNCONDITIONALLY-ISH BUT NEVER GUARDED BY PERMISSION** — `if (window.DeviceOrientationEvent)` registers the handler; iOS requires `requestPermission()` on a user gesture, which this file never requests, so **tilt navigation cannot work on a modern iOS browser** and the failure is silent. (9) **`onKeyDown` USES `e.preventDefault()` ON EVERY ARROW/ENTER/ESCAPE WHEN NO CONTROLLER IS CONNECTED** — with `STATE.enabled` true by default, so on a desktop the module **swallows arrow keys, Enter and Escape globally** the moment `#ch-starred-grid` exists. The guards check `STATE.enabled` and `STATE.connected`, not whether the grid has focus. (10) **Honest strengths:** the platform detection is a real id-substring ladder; `BTN_LABELS` genuinely re-labels per platform (✕○□△ for PlayStation); the `deadZone` is applied on both axes with a dominant-axis tie-break; the focus ring is real (`item.focus({preventScroll:true})`) and syncs to WASM via `SetControllerFocus`; the keyboard fallback covers arrows **and WASD**; and `vibrationActuator` is feature-detected with a try/catch.
- **VERDICT:** ambiguous → a **real, working controller layer with measurable dead code around it**: the two dead grid-type spellings (a third consumer of the `linear-h`/`linear-v` that do not exist), an unread `repeatRate`, an A/B button path with no repeat gate, an unused import and an uncalled haptic engine.


### `tools/archscan/scan.js` — 490 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"Architecture Scanner — Autonomous Flow Detection"* — *"Scans the codebase to detect: 1. Go WASM bridge functions (js.Global().Set) 2. JS ES module imports/exports 3. HTML standalone `<script>` tags 4. CSS SCSS partials 5. Build tag violations 6. Flow integrity (registration + handler pairing). Outputs: tools/archscan/manifest.json."*
- **OWNS:** the `manifest.json` artifact; `scanGoBridge`, `scanJSModules`, `deriveModuleCategory`, `scanHTMLScripts`, `scanSCSSPartials`, `scanBuildTags`, `detectChanges`, `scan`.
- **EXPORTS FOR REUSE:** `module.exports = { scan, scanGoBridge, scanJSModules, scanHTMLScripts, scanSCSSPartials, deriveModuleCategory }` — consumed by `tools/archscan/render.js` to build the generated `architecture.html`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THE `isReferenced` QUESTION THIS TOOLCHAIN ANSWERS IS THE ONE `verify_module_reachability.js` WAS BUILT TO REPLACE, AND BOTH STILL EXIST.** The reachability gate names this family explicitly: *"the metric that looked like it did (**archscan's `isReferenced`**) answers a different question: 'is this path mentioned anywhere?', which a mention INSIDE another unloaded module satisfies. **Referenced is not reachable.**"* This file produces the import/export/binding **census** and `detectChanges` diffs it against the previous manifest — it makes **no reachability claim**, so the two do not contradict. **The weakness lives in the CONSUMER** (`render.js` turns this census into a numbered "Health" score from four arbitrarily-weighted 25-point factors, one defaulting to 100 % when its manifest section is missing) — and that distinction is worth stating, because the scanner itself is honest. (2) **THE FLOW-INTEGRITY PERCENTAGE MEASURES A NAMING CONVENTION, NOT A FLOW GAP.** `js.Global().Set("FuncName"` is matched with `\w+` (no dots, no namespaced names) and the handler regex is `func\s+(Get|Set|Sync|Handle|Toggle)\w*\s*\(this\s+js\.Value` — so a bridge function whose Go implementation is named anything else (this repo sets `triggerCaptureParticles`, `StartMatch`, `AutoBuildDeck`, `RemoveFromDeck` by name) **counts as `registrationOnly`** and drags `integrityPercent` down for a reason that is not a defect; that number is then published as `flowIntegrityPercent`. (3) **`scanBuildTags` CAN ONLY REPORT A MALFORMED TAG, NEVER A WRONG ONE** — it flags a line containing `//go:build` or `// +build` that fails `/^\/\/\s*(go:build|\+build)/`, so a leading-space tag or a contradictory tag set (e.g. `!js && wasm`) passes. The header calls this *"Build tag violations"*; the check is a formatting check. (4) **`glob(GO_DIR, '.go')` IS NON-RECURSIVE AND SCANS THE REPO ROOT ONLY** — `GO_DIR = ROOT`, so `scanGoBridge` and `scanBuildTags` read only root-level `*.go` and silently skip every subdirectory (none exist today, so the census is right, but the walker could not notice one). **`globRecursive` sits in the same file and is used only for SCSS** — the asymmetry is the defect. (5) **`isIIFE` IS ANCHORED TO THE START OF THE FILE** — `/^\s*\(function\s*\(\).test(content)` — so a module with a header comment before its IIFE (which is most of them: `extended_dashboard.js`, `community_dashboard.js`, `life_assets.js` all open with a block comment) reports `isIIFE: false`, and the manifest's `iifeModules` count is under-reported as a fact. (6) **`deriveModuleCategory` IS AN HONEST, DATA-DRIVEN TABLE WITH A STATED EXTENSION POINT** — *"Uses prefix patterns — add new prefixes here as the codebase grows. This is the single source of truth for module categorization"* — with a deterministic fallback chain (prefix → parent directory → `'other'`). Its limit is coverage: most of the app's modules land in `'other'`, so it is a coarse bucket rather than a taxonomy. (7) **`scanHTMLScripts` HARD-CODES ONE FILE** — `const htmlFiles = [path.join(PUBLIC, 'index.html')]` — so `Public/world.html` and every other page are invisible to it, while the reachability gate's `htmlPages()` walks both the root and `Public/`. (8) **THE CHANGE DETECTION IS A USEFUL, BOUNDED DIFF** — added/removed bridge names, added/modified/removed modules by `exportCount`/`importCount`, added/removed script `src`s — with `modified` keyed on the two **counts** only, so a module whose exports changed identity at a constant count is reported unchanged. (9) **The output writes `manifest.json` unconditionally**, so running the scanner is a repo write; the summary and change report are honest and readable.
- **VERDICT:** ambiguous → a **census + diff tool whose scanners are real but coarse** (root-only Go walk, file-start-anchored IIFE test, one HTML page, a `\w+` bridge-name regex feeding a percentage that measures naming), whose *"referenced is not reachable"* weakness is inherited by its consumer `render.js` rather than created here.

- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** **none material — the sweep's model for a served-price progression panel.** Named evidence: (1) **EVERY PRICE COMES FROM THE SERVER** — `kennel.cal` is built from `spawn_fee_micro`, `breed_fee_micro`, `groom_base_micro`, `groom_max_level`, `groom_stat_gain`, `maturity_ms`, and each success message quotes the **served** figure (`kennelVBV(kennel.cal.spawnFee)`, `cal.breedFee`, and `res.fee_micro` straight from the groom response) — *"a client never prices its own upgrade."* (2) **`kennelApi` IMPLEMENTS THE RATE-LIMIT HONESTY RULE WITH THE MANDATE CITED** — *"One-shot retry on HTTP 429, mirroring the Portfolio's rate-limit honesty rule: a refused read is retried once, and if it is still refused the caller must SAY so rather than render 'no companions' (app-entry-mandate §3)."* — and its throw is distinctive and specific: **`'rate-limited — could not be read; try again shortly'`**. (3) **THE REFUSAL IS RENDERED AS A REFUSAL** — `kennelLoad`'s catch writes *"Kennel data could not be read — {message}"* rather than an empty roster. (4) **A `busy` LOCK PREVENTS DOUBLE-SUBMIT ON ALL THREE MONEY DOORS** (`if (kennel.busy) return;` … `finally { kennel.busy = false; }`). (5) **A VANISHED PARENT IS DROPPED, NOT FAKED** — *"A selected parent may have left the roster (sold/adopted) — drop it."* (6) **The eligibility text matches the server's rule** — *"Not eligible to breed (needs mature + certified + legitimate.)"* — which is the §26.4.1 cert-gating the Go sweep recorded inside `BreedPet`. (7) **The power overlay mirrors the server formula with its source quoted** — *"§30 power overlay, mirrored from the server formula (base level + floor(statSum/scale))"* — integer-only (`Math.min(600, base + Math.floor(sum / scale))`), with the scale read from the SERVED `kennel.cal.power_overlay_scale` and a `50` fallback. (8) `kennelVBV` is labelled *"Presentation-boundary micro-$VBV formatting (no ledger value is ever a float)"*. (9) **`kennelGroom` renders `res.stat_gain` as `'?'` when absent** rather than inventing a number.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of companion progression) — **the standard for a served-price progression panel**: every price read from the server and quoted back, the 429 rule implemented with its mandate cited, refusals rendered as refusals, a busy lock on all three doors, and a vanished parent dropped rather than faked.

### `Public/js/particles.js` — 505 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"Public/js/particles.js — PILLAR 5: Visual Feedback & Immersion."* Twelve named effect emitters over one `#particle-canvas`: mood motes, cloak failure, mutation insurance shield, staff-training scan, mutation success, district stabilizer grid, cloak disruptor, contract complete, mutation scar, foundry fusion, global kidnap, capture.
- **OWNS:** `particles`, **`MAX_PARTICLES = 150`**, `isAnimating`, `startAnimationLoop`, `animateParticles`, `initParticleSystem`, and the twelve `triggerXxx` emitters.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** almost every trigger is **ESM-exported AND `window.`-bound** (the ten-line tail publishes them) — `window.triggerCaptureParticles` is bound **twice** (beside its definition and in the tail list), idempotent for a function assignment. `window.initParticleSystem` is bound; **`animateParticles` is neither exported nor bound** (internal).
- **CALLS OUT:** **nothing** — no fetch, no `/api/`; it is driven by the engine and by other modules.
- **DOM/HOST:** requires **`#particle-canvas`**; every emitter early-returns when it is absent.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **A REAL OPERATOR-PRECEDENCE DEFECT AT EIGHT SITES, ALL THE SAME SHAPE: `particles?.length ?? 0 > MAX_PARTICLES`.** `>` binds tighter than `??`, so the expression parses as `particles?.length ?? (0 > MAX_PARTICLES)` — effectively **`particles?.length ?? false`**. It behaves correctly *by accident* (a numeric length is always truthy, so the discarded comparison changes nothing), which is exactly why it has survived: the guard reads as a length check and is in fact a null-coalesce returning the length. **THE FILE'S OWN ANIMATOR WRITES THE CORRECT FORM** — `for (let i = (particles?.length ?? 0) - 1; …)` and `if ((particles?.length ?? 0) > 0)` — so the parenthesised and the broken spellings coexist in one file, the clearest evidence the `??`-mixing rule is not internalised. Same family as `asset_viewer.js`, `early_tasks.js`, `world3d.js` and `constellation_hub.js`. (2) **THE `ctx` BINDING IS OBTAINED AND NEVER USED IN FIVE EMITTERS** — `const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');` then no use of `ctx` in `triggerMoodMote`, `triggerCloakFailureParticles` and three siblings (the renderer obtains its own): a redundant `getContext` per trigger. (3) **`MAX_PARTICLES` IS ENFORCED BY `slice(-MAX_PARTICLES)` — A TAIL TRUNCATION THAT CAN SILENTLY DELETE THE PERSISTENT EFFECTS.** `triggerMutationInsuranceEffect` pushes a **`decay: 0`** shield and `triggerDistrictStabilizerEffect` a **`decay: 0`** grid, both documented *"Persistent until manually removed"* — and because the clamp drops from the FRONT, a burst of 150+ particles **silently discards the shield and the grid**. Each trigger filters its own kind out before re-adding, so a later trigger repairs it, but the removal itself is invisible. Enforcing the cap by kind-weighted eviction rather than by position is the correct shape. (4) **EVERY EMITTER IS `Math.random()`-DRIVEN, AT VOLUME** — `triggerMutationSuccessParticles` rolls 80 particles × ~6 random values, `triggerMutationScarEffect` 110 × ~6, `triggerContractCompleteEffect` 100 × ~6: the Ledger's prohibition does not reach a presentation layer, but a scar effect is ~660 `Math.random()` calls in one synchronous burst. (5) **THREE PLACEHOLDERS ARE HONEST AND LABELLED** — `triggerFoundryFusion(type)`, `triggerGlobalKidnapEffect()` and `triggerCaptureParticles(idx, owner)` **ignore every argument and only call `startAnimationLoop()`**, under the comment *"--- Placeholders for existing system requirements ---"* with *"Implementation for club-specific fusion effects"*. Declared stubs, not fabricated effects — the `counterfeit_scanner.js` standard. (6) **`animateParticles` CORRECTLY SELF-TERMINATES** — when the array empties it sets `isAnimating = false` and does a final `clearRect`, and `startAnimationLoop` guards on `isAnimating`, so **only one rAF cycle is active** (*"startAnimationLoop ensures only one requestAnimationFrame cycle is active."*). That is the opposite of the burn-while-hidden class in `constellation_hub.js`/`world3d.js` — **but the canvas is only cleared when the array empties**, so a *persistent* shield or grid keeps the loop at 60 fps indefinitely. (7) **`initParticleSystem`'s resize guard is genuinely careful** — `if (!parent) return; // canvas detached from DOM (overlay torn down) — skip silently` — the only place in the file where a torn-down canvas is considered. (8) **THE SCANNER EFFECT DOUBLE-ADVANCES `y`** — `p.y += p.vy` in the generic integrator **and again** inside the `isScanner` branch, so a scan line travels at twice its stated velocity. (9) **`triggerMutationScarEffect`'s glitch lines set `vx: rect.width`** — a velocity in the thousands of pixels per frame, intentionally a screen-shake emulation, working because the integrator adds it once and the life decays in ~3 frames.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the particle system) — a complete, correctly-single-loop visual feedback system with honest placeholders and a real cap; its defects are a **`??`-mixing precedence shape at eight sites** (with the correct parenthesised form present in the same file), a **cap enforced by tail-truncation that can silently drop the two persistent effects**, and a double-advanced scanner velocity.

### `Public/js/network.js` — 542 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"Public/js/network.js"* — **the WebSocket rail**: connect, reconnect with backoff, the identity watchdog, and the **entire server→client event dispatch table**.
- **OWNS:** `socket`, `myClientId`, `reconnectAttempts`, `nonceResolver`, `identitySyncTimeout`, `lastPingTime`, `currentLatency`, `reconnectBackoff`, and the batched-sync scheduler (`syncScheduled`, `currentSyncScope`). Seven setters + five getters export them.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** ESM exports (`initWebSocket`, `handleServerMessage`, `sendPing`, `requestMatchSync`, `getNonceResolver`, the state setters/getters) + **`window.sendPing`**, **`window.requestMatchSync`**, **`window.onNonceResponse`**.
- **CALLS OUT:** `CONFIG` (and **mutates it from the `identity` payload**), `wallet.js initWalletConnect`, `ui.js` handlers, `game.js`/`economy.js`/`admin.js`/`criminality.js` consumers, and ~40 WASM bridge globals by name (`SyncFullProfile`, `SyncVaultBalance`, `SyncSolvency`, `SyncRewards`, `SyncClubs`, `SyncPortfolio`, `SyncTournament`, `SyncCardMetadata`, `SyncOpponentDeck`, `StartMatch`, `SetAvatar`, `SetLocalPlayerIndex`, …).
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **A REAL SHAPE DEFECT IN `requestMatchSync`: THE CLOSING BRACE IS MIS-PLACED, SO `window.requestMatchSync = requestMatchSync;` SITS INSIDE THE FUNCTION BODY.** The assignment line has **no indentation** and directly precedes the function's own `}` (`…socket.send(JSON.stringify({…}));\nwindow.requestMatchSync = requestMatchSync;\n}`). It parses, so the assignment happens **on every CALL** rather than at load — which means **`window.requestMatchSync` is undefined until the first call**, and its only caller is the WASM engine reaching for it when it detects a sequence gap: exactly the case where it does not yet exist. `js.Global().Call` on a missing global throws. (2) **THE `identity` PAYLOAD REWRITES `CONFIG` AND THEN CALLS `initWalletConnect()`** — `CONFIG.VAULT_ADDRESS`, `VBV_ASSET_ID`, `AVOI_ASSET_ID`, `WC_PROJECT_ID` are overwritten from the message with *"[CONFIG] Authoritative environment synced from server."*: a client config object mutated by a WebSocket message. The `WC_PROJECT_ID` arriving after an early failed init is the path that makes the modal work, since `initWalletConnect` returns early once `signClient` exists. (3) **THE IDENTITY WATCHDOG FORCES A RECONNECT ON A 5-SECOND TIMER** — `setTimeout(…, 5000)` closing the socket if `myClientId` is unset, with a one-time `reconnectAttempts === 1` toast to prevent spam; `reconnectBackoff` (3000) is declared, read, and reset on a successful identity. (4) **THE `identity` CASE DOES NOT RESOLVE THE NONCE RESOLVER — AND THE FILE SAYS SO WITH THE REASON** — *"WS consumer (flow-doc §12.3): the nonce push is what actually resolves the pending wallet/admin nonce promise (the identity message does NOT call the resolver)."* That comment is the 2026-09-09 (c) flow-doc correction preserved at the site. (5) **ALL NINE PREVIOUSLY-DROPPED EVENTS NOW HAVE CASES, PLUS A `default`** — `rivalry_update`, `investment_confirmed`, `investment_update`, `dividend_claimed`, `creator_royalty_paid`, `creator_royalty_received`, `career_tier_demoted`, `link_wallet_response`, `nonce_response`, each routing to `window.on<Event>`, with `default` forwarding to `window.__vbtWsDispatch` under the comment *"— these backend-emitted events previously had NO case and NO default → silently dropped."* (6) **THE BATCHED-SYNC SCHEDULER IS A REAL, DOCUMENTED OPTIMISATION** — *"Batches UI synchronization requests using requestAnimationFrame. This prevents layout thrashing and redundant DOM diffing when multiple WebSocket messages arrive within the same frame"* — with `"all"` swallowing any granular scope (`if (currentSyncScope === "all") return;`). (7) **`lobby_update` QUERIES THE ENGINE ONCE, EARLY, AND USES THE VALUE LATE** — `const state = window.GetGameState("combat");` near the top of the case, then `if (state && state.phase === "Active")` at the end to pick the sync scope — so a `SyncFullProfile` performed **inside this same handler** cannot affect the scope chosen at its end. (8) **TWO UNGUARDED `getElementById` DEREFERENCES IN THE `season_end` BRANCH** — `document.getElementById("season-num-display").innerText = …` and `document.getElementById("season-countdown-widget").classList.remove("hidden")` are written without a null check, so a missing id throws mid-dispatch and aborts the remainder of the `lobby_update` handler. (9) **`handleAchievementUnlock` HAS A REAL DEDUP GUARD** — `lastAchievementId` plus a 2-second clear, with the reason stated (*"Deduplicate rapid-fire unlocks of the same achievement"*). (10) **`currentRewardRatio` IS ASSIGNED HERE AND DECLARED NOWHERE IN THIS FILE** — `currentRewardRatio = msg.payload.RewardRatio; // PILLAR 2: Update global for scaled payouts` — an implicit global, since this module carries no `'use strict'`; the exact pattern that would throw if one were added.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the WebSocket rail) — the file holding the reconnect backoff, the identity watchdog, the batched-sync scheduler and the full dispatch table with its nine-event fix recorded in place; its defects are a **mis-placed closing brace leaving `window.requestMatchSync` undefined until first call**, **two unguarded `getElementById` writes in the `season_end` branch**, and an **implicit global** (`currentRewardRatio`).


### `Public/js/game_multiplayer.js` — 616 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"game_multiplayer.js — Real-Time P2P Multiplayer Controller"* — *"Integrates with existing game.js and network.js WebSocket infrastructure. Adds real-time move sync, latency tracking, in-match chat, and connection status."*
- **OWNS:** **`#wd-game`** (the World Dashboard's `multiplayer` panel — the one panel session (f) recorded as rendering empty until match state exists, and this file is why), the whole `mp*` state block (`mpConnected`, `mpMatchId`, `mpOpponentId/Name/Avatar`, `mpIsHost`, `mpLatency`, `mpBoardState` — a 9-slot array, `mpMyDeck`, `mpOpponentDeck`, `mpChatMessages`, `mpGameState`), and eleven render/attach functions.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** `export function initGameMultiplayer` + **`window.initGameMultiplayer`, `window.handleMultiplayerMessage`, `window.startPingInterval`** — the last consumed by `network.js`'s `mp_move`/`mp_chat`/`mp_forfeit`/`mp_opponent_*`/`mp_game_over` cases and by `matchmaking_status`.
- **CALLS OUT:** sends `join_queue`, `create_room`, `join_room`, **`mp_move`**, **`mp_chat`**, **`mp_forfeit`** and `ping` (with a payload `timestamp`) over the shared socket; reads `window.GetGameState('all')`, `window.getMatchHistory()`, `window.showToast`.
- **DOM/HOST:** requires `#wd-game`; hosts `#mp-connection-status`, `#mp-wallet-address`, `#mp-server-indicator`, `#mp-latency-value`, `#mp-find-match-btn`, `#mp-create-room-btn`, `#mp-join-room-btn`, `#mp-matchmaking-status`, `#mp-history`, `#mp-chat-input`, `#mp-chat-send`, `#mp-forfeit-btn`, `.mp-board-tile`, `.mp-hand-card`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **A REAL LOGIC INVERSION IN `onGameOver`: THE WIN TEST IS BACKWARDS.** `const won = payload.winner === mpOpponentId;` then `window.showToast(won ? '🎉 You won!' : '😤 You lost!', …)` — **a payload whose `winner` IS the opponent is reported as "You won"**. Every multiplayer match congratulates the loser and commiserates the winner. It is the `justice_handlers.go` / `season_countdown.js` class in its purest form: a decision variable computed with the wrong polarity and consumed immediately. (2) **`renderChatMessages` INTERPOLATES CHAT TEXT RAW INTO `innerHTML` — an injection path from another player.** `…<span class="mp-chat-sender">${msg.sender}:</span><span class="mp-chat-text">${msg.text}</span>` — fed by **`onChatMessage(payload)`'s `payload.text` off the socket**, i.e. text authored by a **remote peer**, rendered with no escaping. The file applies no `esc()` anywhere. Highest-severity finding in the file. (3) **`mpBoardState` IS A 9-SLOT INDEXED ARRAY WITH NO BOUNDS CHECK ON EITHER SIDE OF THE WIRE.** `placeCard(tileIndex)` reads `mpBoardState[tileIndex]` from `parseInt(tile.dataset.index)` (safe locally, rendered from a 9-iteration map) while **`onOpponentMove(payload)` writes `mpBoardState[payload.tile_index] = card` with the index taken straight from the peer** — an out-of-range index silently extends the array and a negative one is equally unvalidated. (4) **`placeCard` DOES AN OPTIMISTIC UPDATE WITH NO ROLLBACK** — `mpBoardState[tileIndex] = card; mpMyDeck.splice(mpSelectedCard, 1); mpMyTurn = false;` under the comment *"Optimistic update"* — so a server refusal (not your turn, stale `match_id`) leaves the card consumed and the turn spent locally; only a later `onStateSync` can repair it. (5) **`createRoom` GENERATES THE ROOM CODE CLIENT-SIDE WITH `Math.random()`** — `Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 8).toUpperCase()`, a 6-character code from a non-cryptographic source, **announced to the player before the server has accepted it** (`"Room ${roomId} created!"`). Two clients can collide and the success toast precedes any acknowledgement. (6) **`renderMatchHistory` READS `window.getMatchHistory()` WITH A `typeof` GUARD** — *"Fetch from matchHistory via game.js"* — so a missing hook renders *"No recent matches"* rather than throwing: an honest degradation. (7) **`startPingInterval`'s `setInterval` IS NEVER STORED OR CLEARED** — the exported starter returns nothing and holds no handle, so repeated calls stack intervals, each sending a `ping` every 5 s. It is also **the only heartbeat carrying `payload.timestamp`**, while `network.js`'s own `sendPing` sends `{type:"ping"}` and measures from `lastPingTime`: **two pings, two latency conventions**, and `mpLatency` depends on the server echoing `timestamp` back. (8) **`mpConnected`, `mpOpponentConnected`, `mpMyTurn`, `mpIsHost` AND `mpOpponentDeck` ARE ASSIGNED AND NEVER READ** in any render path (`mpOpponentConnected` is set by two handlers and read nowhere) — declared state with no consumer. (9) **`getSocket()` PREFERS THE IMPORTED BINDING AND FALLS BACK TO `window.socket`** — `if (networkSocket) return networkSocket;` — and `network.js` exports `socket` as a `let`, so the import is a **live binding** the module reassigns on every reconnect; the global fallback would read a stale value. The binding choice is correct and worth recording as such. (10) **Honest strengths:** every send is preceded by a `readyState !== WebSocket.OPEN` refusal with a toast; `placeCard` checks `mpMyTurn`, tile occupancy and card selection **before** sending; `forfeitMatch` requires `confirm()`; `onStateSync` treats the server's board as authoritative; and the `#wd-game` guard in `initGameMultiplayer` correctly leaves the panel alone when absent.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the P2P multiplayer panel) — a complete move-sync controller whose three real defects are an **inverted win test in `onGameOver`**, **unescaped peer-authored chat text interpolated into `innerHTML`**, and an **unbounded server-supplied tile index written into the board array**; plus a leaked ping interval and five declared-but-unread state variables.


### `Public/js/slide_theming.js` — 546 lines
- **PURPOSE:** ***"slide_theming.js — §10.6 THE APP'S SLIDESHOWS (boot / main menu + World Dashboard)"*** — *"Two shows, three slides each, gentle fade between them … EVERY slide shows the placeholder pack by default (placeholder_assets.js), and EVERY slide can be re-themed by the viewer with one of their OWN bonded assets."* The header names all four routes it uses and states its own contract: *"This module is PRESENTATION ONLY: it paints what the server says to paint and never decides who owns what. It writes no branding, sends nothing to the server at render time, and if a read is refused it keeps the last known art AND says the read failed (a refusal is never rendered as 'no theme')."*
- **OWNS:** the two shows (`menu`, `dashboard`), `stState` (slots, policy, capacity, derivatives, shows, starter), `stUiTrees` (§10.7 assignment cache), `stSafeUri`, `stApi`, `paint`, `setIndex`, `mount`/`unmount`/`pause`/`resume`, `describe()`.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** **`window.SlideTheming`** (a 20-key API incl. `refresh`, `ensureStarter`, `setSlot`, `clearSlot`, `clearAll`, `describe`, `onChange`, `mount`, `unmount`, `pause`, `resume`, `paint`, `slotViews`, **`loadUiTrees`, `paintUiTrees`, `uiTrees`**, `preferLight`, `lightProbe`, `state`, `BOOT_SLOTS`) + `window.mountBootSlides` / `window.mountDashboardSlides` + a 13-name ESM export; mounted by `menu-constellation.js` (*"window.SlideTheming.mount('menu', bgLayer)"*) and `world_dashboard.js`.
- **CALLS OUT:** **`GET|POST /api/assets/slide-theme`**, **`POST /api/assets/slide-theme/clear`**, **`GET /api/assets/catalogue`**, **`POST /api/assets/starter`**, **`GET /api/assets/ui-trees`** — all through `stApi`, which **appends the wallet query parameter itself**.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** **none material — the sweep's cleanest viewer-scoped renderer, with its discipline stated in the file rather than assumed.** Named evidence: (1) **`stSafeUri` REFUSES EVERYTHING A BROWSER CANNOT LOAD, AND SAYS SO** — *"Only art a browser can actually load is painted: http(s) URLs and same-origin /Assets/ paths. Everything else (data:, blob:, javascript:, ipfs://, ar:// without a gateway) is refused here as well as server-side — we never invent a gateway."* — two anchored regexes, so `data:`/`blob:`/`javascript:`/content-addressed schemes all return `''`. (2) **THE WALLET IS APPENDED BY THE HELPER, NOT BY EACH CALLER** — so no call site can forget it, the class `life_assets.js`'s `walletQS()` exists to fix. (3) **A WALLET CHANGE INVALIDATES THE CACHE** — *"A wallet that differs from the one the last read was for INVALIDATES the cache"* — the stated reason the read is keyed on `stState.wallet`. (4) **THE ONE-SHOT 429 RETRY IS THE ESTABLISHED RULE** (retry once after 450 ms, mirroring the Portfolio/Kennel). (5) **`adoptSlots` LETS THE SERVER WIN** — *"replaces the painted table with the served surface: the SERVER wins, so a server-side change to a slot, its default or its rule is never overruled by this client's boot fallback."* (6) **THE BOOT FALLBACK IS NAMED AND TIMED** — *"painted BEFORE the first read settles, so the boot screen is never blank"* — and `default_derived`/`default_source_uri`/`default_note` are carried per slot so the studio and probes can always say **which shipped frame** a slide shows and whether it is the LIGHT rendition. (7) **THE CYCLE SKIPS WORK INVISIBLY AND SAYS WHY** — `if (document.hidden || show.paused || show.host.offsetParent === null) return;` with *"The tick is skipped while the browser tab is hidden or the host is not in the layout, so a slideshow behind another overlay costs nothing (the same discipline the constellation-hub particles follow)."* (8) **`mount` IS IDEMPOTENT PER HOST** (`existing.host === host && existing.root && host.contains(existing.root)` → repaint and return) and `unmount` clears the interval and removes the node. (9) **§10.7 UI-TREE PAINTING NEVER GUESSES** — *"an unmarked or unassigned tree is left alone (ownership/naming is never guessed)"* — a **missing** tree id goes into a `missing[]` list, so `marked`/`painted`/`missing` is a real census (which is what caught the two un-art-ed trees in session (d)), and `data-wd-tree-sku` is set beside the CSS property. (10) **`stNotify` SWALLOWS A LISTENER ERROR WITH ITS REASON** — *"a listener must not break the slideshow"* — the deliberate counterpart to `user_preferences.js`'s silent `notify()`, stating the tradeoff in place. (11) **`describe()` PUBLISHES A REAL CENSUS** (slots/themed/stale, `shows` with `layers`/`painted`/`active`/`visible`, `derivedSlides`, the full `uiTrees` block) for the probes, every value read from state rather than recomputed.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of §10.6/§10.7 rendering) — **the model for a viewer-scoped art renderer**: a URI allowlist that invents no gateway, a wallet the helper never lets a caller forget, a server-wins adoption rule, a named boot fallback, an invisible-work skip with its reason, and a `marked/painted/missing` census that made another session's defect visible.


### `Public/world.html` — 565 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"NFT-Seduction — 3D World"* — the standalone 3D page at `/world`: a Three.js scene with a capsule avatar, ground plane + grid, five territory markers, a HUD (top bar, region indicator, controls help, nearby-entity list, minimap canvas, travel menu, bottom bar) and its own inline `<script type="module">`.
- **OWNS:** `#world-canvas`, `#world-loading`, the whole HUD, its OWN `<style>` block (~100 lines) and its OWN Three.js scene/camera/renderer/avatar/minimap/animation loop.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** the page itself plus four inline `onclick` handlers — `window.close()`, `toggleTravel()`, `interact()`, `openMenu()` — and `travelTo('base'|'north'|'east'|'south'|'west'|'club')`, bound as `window.travelTo`.
- **CALLS OUT:** **NOTHING — there is no `fetch`, no `/api/` string and no WebSocket anywhere in the file.** The wallet is read from `localStorage.getItem('wallet_address')`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THE ENTIRE WORLD IS STATIC — and this settles the `/world` question `constellation_hub.js` raised.** `const territories = [{ name:'Base', x:0, z:0, color:0x6366f1 }, { name:'North' … }, …]` is a **hard-coded five-entry array**, `state.nearbyEntities` is never populated from any source, and the entity list renders `state.nearbyEntities.slice(0, 6)` — so **"NEARBY ENTITIES" is always empty** and the minimap draws only the five constants plus the player. The world is visually complete and data-empty. (2) **THE WALLET IS READ FROM `localStorage['wallet_address']`, A KEY THE REST OF THE APP DOES NOT USE.** The wallet rail stores `vbabes_linked_wallets` and `vbabes_payout_address` (`wallet.js`) and exposes `userAddress`/`getActiveWallet`; `wallet_address` appears nowhere else, so the top-bar wallet shows `0x----...----` for every connected player and `state.wallet` stays `''`. The `try/catch` around it is correct and silent. (3) **THE LOADING SCREEN IS HIDDEN BY A 1-SECOND TIMER, NOT BY READINESS** — `setTimeout(() => document.getElementById('world-loading').classList.add('hidden'), 1000)` with no check that the scene built: the `showMatchDetails`/countdown class in a milder form (a fixed belief about when work finishes). (4) **THE PAGE HAS ITS OWN IMPORTMAP AND ITS OWN THREE.JS, so it is a SECOND COMPOSITION ROOT outside the Single-Entry Mandate.** The page-declared-scripts rule accommodates it (the reachability gate treats a page's own `src` as a root), but it means the `world` destination **duplicates a renderer `world3d.js` also owns: two 3D engines**, one embedded and one on a separate page, reached from the same hub through two mechanisms (`window.enter3DWorld` vs `window.location.href = '/world'`). (5) **`updateMinimap` AND `updateEntityList` RUN EVERY FRAME** — `animate()` calls `updateMovement`, `updateMinimap`, `updateEntityList` and `renderer.render` on every `requestAnimationFrame` with **no visibility pause**, in contrast to the discipline `slide_theming.js`, `constellation_hub.js` and `world3d.js` all apply: the minimap re-fills a 160×160 canvas and rewrites `innerHTML` 60 times a second whether or not anything changed. (6) **THE TERRITORY → POSITION TABLE IS DECLARED TWICE** — once as the `territories` array and again inside `travelTo` as a `positions` object with the same five keys **plus `club`** — so moving a territory needs two edits and the `club` destination exists in only one of them (the marker list has no `club`). (7) **`travelTo` REPOSITIONS AND RELABELS, AND NOTHING ELSE** — it sets `playerGroup.position` and writes `#world-region`; there is no region state, no request and no persistence, so travel is purely visual. (8) **`openMenu()` DELEGATES BY FOCUS, NOT NAVIGATION** — `if (window.opener) window.opener.focus();` under the comment *"Open menu overlay or redirect to main menu"*: the comment describes two behaviours and the code implements a third, so "☰ Menu" does nothing when the page was opened directly. (9) **Escaping is absent but there is nothing dynamic to escape** — `updateEntityList` interpolates `${e.icon}`/`${e.name}` and the array is empty, so the missing `esc()` is latent rather than live.
- **VERDICT:** ambiguous → **a standalone 3D page that is a second composition root and a second renderer**: a complete HUD and scene with no data source at all (hard-coded territories, an always-empty entity list, a `localStorage` key nothing else writes), a readiness-by-timer loading screen, a doubled territory table, and a per-frame minimap/entity repaint with no visibility pause.

(8) **`renderDividendTracker`/`renderPortfolioHoldings` ARE WIRED**, but the tracker only refreshes from its own tab actions and the WS consumer, so a claim made elsewhere is not reflected until one of those fires.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the Entity Investment overlay) — a four-tab investor surface with a real refresh guard, a real boot-race retry, a correct HTML escaper and three wired WS consumers; its blocking defect is a **stale read contract on `/api/invest/portfolio`** (the second consumer of a route already repaired once elsewhere), plus a **vault-fallback wallet resolver** and an unescaped id in an inline handler.
