- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THE SAMPLE-ITEM DEFECT IS FIXED HERE AND THE FIX IS RECORDED WITH ITS CONSEQUENCE — session (e)'s repair, at the site:** *"SOURCED FROM THE ONE TAXONOMY (window.WDTaxonomy, published read-only by world_dashboard.js). It used to be a hard-coded list of six invented ids ('world','battle','justice','economy','faith','pets'): the preview showed categories the game does not have, and the per-button override panel keyed its rows to those same ids, so an override set there could NEVER match a real button (real ids are 'player','careers','assets',…). Falls back to a placeholder ONLY if the dashboard has not been composed yet."* `sampleItems()` reads the frozen taxonomy first and `SAMPLE_FALLBACK` now holds six **real** ids. (2) **THE LAYOUT CLASSIFICATION DELEGATES TO ONE OWNER, AND ITS LOCAL FALLBACK USES THE CORRECT SPELLINGS** — `isPositioned` prefers `MenuCustomization.isPositionedGrid` else `!['grid','linearH','linearV'].includes(gridType)`; `isRadial` falls back to `['circle','arc','spokes']`. **`linearH`/`linearV` are the REAL keys** per session (e)'s measurement — so this file, unlike `controller_nav.js`, spells them right even in the fallback. (3) **THE PREVIEW APPLIES THE SAME SPIN TRANSFORM THE LIVE MENU DOES, AND SAYS SO** — *"The spin is a CSS rotation of the RING with each item counter-rotated so labels stay upright — exactly the transform the live menu applies, so the preview is not a different visual rule from the thing it previews."* — gated identically (`isAbsolute && isRadial(config.gridType)`). (4) **`export function renderPerButtonList() { /* Rendered by buildPanel */ }` IS AN EXPORTED EMPTY FUNCTION** — a declared API with an empty body whose comment says the panel renders it instead; `selectPerButton` calls it then `renderPreview()`, so a caller relying on it does nothing. (5) **`testController()` AND THE `.mc-test-controller-btn` HANDLER BOTH ONLY TOAST** — *"🎮 Controller test: rumble activated!"* — **the rumble is not activated**: `controller_nav.js` owns a real `hapticFeedback` engine with three profiles one module away, and this panel neither calls it nor is connected to that module. A control asserting an effect it does not perform. (6) **THE CONTROLLER MAPPINGS ARE A SECOND, HARD-CODED TABLE THAT CONTRADICTS THE CONTROLLER LAYER** — `renderControllerMappings()` declares **X → Quick Menu, Y → Favorites, LB → Prev Tab, RB → Next Tab**, while `controller_nav.js` reads only `A` (select), `B` (back), the D-pad and the left stick and binds **no tab-switching at all**. The panel documents controls the product does not implement. (7) **`importMenuCustomization` REPLACES `currentConfig` WITH RAW JSON AND VALIDATES NOTHING** — `currentConfig = JSON.parse(json)` then `updateUIFromConfig()` + `renderPreview()`; a parseable-but-malformed object reaches `computePositions` (which has its own try/catch) and `saveConfig` would persist it. (8) **`saveConfig` WRITES THE WHOLE CONFIG IN ONE CALL** — `UserPreferences.setMenuLayout(currentConfig)` — the shallow-merge path `user_preferences.js` records as carrying no per-key migration; the panel at least supplies every key it knows. (9) **`open()` RE-READS THE DEFAULTS ON EVERY OPEN** (`currentConfig = getDefaultConfig()`), discarding unsaved edits — correct Cancel semantics, and Save/Reset/Cancel are all three bound. (10) **Honest strengths:** the overlay is contained (`overlay vbt-overlay`, inline reveal, `close()` calls `hideAllOverlays()` first); `buildPanel()` is inserted once and `bindEvents()` runs once; and the tail auto-init is guarded on the overlay already existing.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the menu customization panel) — **the repaired file**: sample ids come from the one taxonomy with the old defect recorded in place, the layout classification delegates correctly with the right fallback spellings, and the preview applies the real spin transform; its remaining defects are an **empty exported `renderPerButtonList`**, a **"Test Controller" control that toasts a rumble it never triggers**, and a **second hard-coded controller mapping table contradicting `controller_nav.js`**.


### `tools/server/verify_ui_handlers.js` — 608 lines
- **PURPOSE:** ***"verify_ui_handlers.js — THE INLINE-HANDLER GATE."*** Its header states the failure mode it exists for: *"An inline handler (`onclick="openThing()"`) resolves `openThing` on `window`. A module-scope function is NOT a global, so a handler whose name nothing publishes throws `ReferenceError` and the control does absolutely NOTHING — no error surface, no toast, no network call. That is how EIGHT Admin Suite controls were dead until 2026-09-15, and it is a SYSTEMIC failure mode."*
- **TWO INDEPENDENT TIERS, WITH THE REASON STATED:** *"neither alone is complete"* — **STATIC** (parse every `on<event>="…"` in `Public/**` and compare against every `window.X =` / `globalThis.X =` / `Object.assign(window, {…})` publication) and **BROWSER** (*"evaluate `typeof window[name]` for every extracted name … This is authoritative: it catches a name published in a module that never evaluated, and a publication that assigned a non-function"*). **And the verdict rule is the point:** *"A name that is unpublished-but-bound, or bound-but-not-loaded, is still DEAD to the user. Exit code is 1 when any handler name is dead, so this can gate a build."*
- **OWNS:** `EVENTS` (32 event names, deliberately broad — *"a missed event is a hole"*), `ATTR_RE`, `KEYWORDS`, `BUILTIN_GLOBALS`, `commentRanges`/`inRanges` (a small tokenizer — *"Documentation that MENTIONS a handler … must never be read as a live control"*), `readAttribute`, `collectPublications`, **`collectWasmGlobals`**, **`reachableModules`**, `definitionIndex`, `class CDP`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS / MERITS:** **the second-strongest gate in the family, and its four most interesting mechanisms are all deliberate.** (1) **COMMENTS ARE TOKENIZED OUT** — a match inside a comment is *counted* (`ignoredInComments`) rather than reported, because `admin_suite.js`'s own header *documents* `onclick="adminX()"` as the defect it fixed. (2) **CONCATENATED VALUES ARE COUNTED, NOT GUESSED** — `if (!value.trim()) { splitValues++; continue; }` and the report line reads `(+N built by concatenation — not parsed)`, so a handler built at runtime is declared unmeasured instead of silently passed. (3) **IT KNOWS THE THREE PUBLICATION IDIOMS**, including the one `admin_suite.js` introduced: `Object.entries(TABLE).forEach(([name, fn]) => { window[name] = fn; })` has **no literal `window.X =`**, so the code locates the TABLE by name and takes its keys — with the reason in place. (4) **IT SEPARATES THREE DEADNESS REASONS AND ONLY ONE IS A FAILURE** — unpublished (`dead`), published-but-not-evaluated, and **`reachableModules()`** (a BFS over relative imports from `app.js`) which classifies a name published from a module outside the composition as **NOT-COMPOSED** rather than broken, *"its markup cannot render either"* — exactly the distinction session (d) established as *referenced ≠ reachable*. (5) **`definitionIndex()` MAKES THE REPORT ACTIONABLE** — *"so the report can tell a handler that merely lacks a publisher from markup that names a function nothing ever defined"* — and that distinction found the six Class-2 names (`window.cleanupSocialHub` throwing before its own `.remove()`). (6) **THE NOTES ARE CLASSIFIED, NOT FAILED** — a name a boot-time read cannot see (4 lazily published, 4 on another page) is a NOTE with its reason and the summary groups them, so the gate reports **DEAD 0** while still naming what it could not verify. (7) **THE BROWSER TIER CARRIES BUSINESS EVIDENCE, NOT JUST NAME RESOLUTION** — `engine readiness observed`, `boot console/page errors` and an `admin surface evidence` line (`present=… computed=… declaredControls=… binder=…`), which is what the SCSS audit used as its regression proof. (8) **`resolveChrome()` HAS FIVE CANDIDATES** (env var, two Chrome paths, LOCALAPPDATA Chrome, two Edge paths) and `main()` exits **2** on a probe failure versus **1** on dead handlers — three distinct exit codes. (9) **`waitFor` POLLS** `httpGet` every 300 ms rather than sleeping a fixed interval. **Honest limits stated by the file:** `${…}` interpolations are stripped before extraction (an unstripped scan reported 44 false dead names for `esc()` alone), a name built by concatenation is counted but not parsed, and the browser tier requires a running dev server (hence `--static`).
- **VERDICT:** owner — **the inline-handler gate**, and the family's best example of *classifying* rather than merely counting: comments tokenized out, concatenation declared unmeasured, three publication idioms known (including the table-publish loop), three deadness reasons separated so only one fails, a boot-time-unreadable name downgraded to a reasoned NOTE, and the browser tier returning business evidence beside name resolution.


### `Public/js/audio.js` — 785 lines
- **PURPOSE:** no header block — the **Web Audio rail**: a low-latency SFX engine, a music/ambient transition system, and ~40 named playback functions across PILLARS 1/3/4/5/6.
- **OWNS:** `masterVolume`/`musicVolume`/`sfxVolume` + their `last*Volume` siblings (six exported floats persisted in `localStorage`), `audioCtx`, `sfxGainNode`, `musicGainNode`, **the master `DynamicsCompressor`**, `bufferCache` (url → Promise), `sfxCooldowns` + `MIN_SFX_INTERVAL = 50`, `MUSIC_PHASE_MAP` (8 phases → track names), `currentMusicSource`/`currentMusicGain`, `currentMutationSoundscapeSource`, `currentMutationInsuranceHumSource`, `currentDistrictStabilizerThrumSource`.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** **27 `window.*` bindings** at the tail (`window.PlaySound = playSFX`, `window.initAudioContext`, and every `play*`/`stop*` function) plus their ESM exports — the engine calls several by name.
- **CALLS OUT:** `CONFIG` (imported) and `localStorage`; **no `fetch` and no `/api/`** — audio files load through `getSFXBuffer(url)` into `bufferCache`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **A REAL ROUTING DEFECT: `transitionMusic` BYPASSES THE MUSIC GAIN NODE AND THE COMPRESSOR.** Its new track does `newGain.connect(audioCtx.destination); // Connect to master destination` — **`audioCtx.destination`, not `musicGainNode`** — while `initAudioContext` builds `sfxGainNode → compressor` and `musicGainNode → compressor` and calls `syncMusicGain()`. So **every cross-faded ambient track skips both the music bus and the master compressor**, and the compressor's own stated purpose (*"prevent digital clipping during high-frequency combat events"*) does not apply to music at all; the track also ramps to `musicVolume * masterVolume` on its own gain, duplicating what `musicGainNode` exists for. (2) **A SECOND AUDIO OWNER EXISTS AND THIS FILE NEVER MENTIONS IT.** The sweep recorded three audio owners (`audio.js`, `audio_context.js`, `audio_engine.js`); this file binds **`window.initAudioContext`** while `audio_context.js` owns `initAudioContextManager`, and both create their own `AudioContext` with no detection or deference. (3) **`playMoodMoteSFX` THROTTLES WITH `Math.random()`** — `if (Math.random() > 0.05) return;` under *"Audio triggers on only ~5% of visual events"* — presentation-layer, but it means the sound descends from the visual event it accompanies rather than being the same event, and is not reproducible. (4) **`transitionMusic`'s `isMusicTransitioning` GUARD LEAKS ON EVERY EARLY RETURN** — set `true` before `if (!audioCtx) initAudioContext();`, cleared only at the **end** of the success path, while the `await audioCtx.resume()` failure path returns early (`catch(e) { return; }`) and `if (!buffer || !audioCtx) return;` is a second: **after ONE failed buffer load this function returns immediately for the rest of the session and music can never change again**, silently. (5) **`localStorage.setItem('currentMusicTrack', …)` IS THE CROSS-FADE DEDUP KEY** — `const currentTrack = localStorage.getItem('currentMusicTrack'); if (currentTrack === trackName) return;` — so "already playing" is a **persisted string**, written only after the buffer loaded (correct for a failed load) but never cleared by a stop. (6) **VOLUME STATE IS SIX EXPORTED MUTABLE FLOATS READ FROM `localStorage` AT MODULE LOAD**, each `last*Volume` falling back to the current value if non-zero else `'0.5'`: the mute/unmute restore behaviour is really implemented, but the authority is `localStorage` rather than an engine value. (7) **`sfxCooldowns` + `MIN_SFX_INTERVAL = 50` IS A REAL DE-DUPLICATION GUARD** (map path → timestamp, 50 ms) — the one place identical rapid events are deliberately collapsed. (8) **`MUSIC_PHASE_MAP` IS AN EIGHT-ENTRY PHASE VOCABULARY** (`DISCONNECTED`/`Setup`/`Lobby`/`TournamentLobby`/`Active_Casual`/`Active_Quick`/`Active_Tournament`/`Finished` → track filenames) whose keys are the **client's own phase names** — the only declaration of that vocabulary in the sweep, with no server counterpart. (9) **The loading path is careful** — `bufferCache` stores the PROMISE (so concurrent calls share one decode), a failed load is **deleted from the cache** (*"Clear failed load from cache"*), and the decode is awaited inside an async factory. (10) **The three long-running sources each have a scoped guard** (`if (currentXSource) return;`) and a matching `stop*` that nulls the handle — the looping-hum family is correctly single-instance. (11) **`playCharacterVoiceLine`'s `characterType` REACHES ONLY A PATH LOOKUP** while the docstring names five archetypes (`"Witch"`, `"Boss"`, `"Lady"`, `"cute"`, `"Mini-Boss"`); an unknown archetype resolves to a generic file or nothing, so the parameter is decorative beyond the two named cases.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the SFX/music rail) — a real Web Audio engine with a master compressor, a promise-keyed buffer cache that evicts failures, per-source single-instance guards and a cooldown map; its defects are a **music path connected straight to `audioCtx.destination`, bypassing `musicGainNode` and the compressor**, and a **transition guard that leaks on the early-return paths so one failed track load permanently disables music changes**.


### `Public/wasm_exec.js` — 575 lines — PROVENANCE (Go toolchain file, read not mapped in detail)
- **PROVENANCE:** **NOT first-party.** It is the Go distribution's WebAssembly runtime glue, copied verbatim: the file's own first two lines are *"Copyright 2018 The Go Authors. All rights reserved. Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style license that can be found in the LICENSE file."* Its structure (`globalThis.fs` shim, `globalThis.process` shim, the `crypto`/`performance`/`TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` preconditions, `globalThis.Go = class { … }` with `setInt64`, `_scheduledTimeouts`, `_nextCallbackTimeoutID`) is the unmodified upstream implementation.
- **WHY IT SITS AT `Public/`:** the Single-Entry Mandate names it explicitly as one of the few things `index.html` may load directly — *"`wasm_exec.js` (the Go/WASM glue)"* — and both gates encode that: `verify_module_reachability.js` keeps it in SKIP_FILES (a composition root, not a module) and `verify_ui_handlers.js` keeps it in SKIP_FILES too (it publishes `globalThis.Go`, not handlers).
- **READ TREATMENT:** **PROVENANCE, not a full map.** Its 575 lines are upstream Go source with zero project-authored logic, so mapping them as app surface would be noise; the two reads taken (1-120 plus the head bytes) establish the copyright header, the shim set and the `Go` class entry to confirm it is unmodified. **A file copied from a toolchain should be recorded as such rather than analysed** — this entry substitutes for a line-by-line row, and the coverage ledger records it as `provenance`.
- **THE ONE THING WORTH CHECKING:** the Go/WASM pairing is **version-coupled** — `wasm_exec.js` must match the Go toolchain that built `Public/main.wasm`, and a mismatch produces a `Go` class that cannot instantiate the module. The sweep's repeated measurements of `Public/main.wasm` (11,375,951 B, mtime 09/16 11:50) and of the three build targets are the evidence that this pairing is currently consistent.


### `Public/js/npc_taunts.js` — 815 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"npc_taunts.js — NPC Taunts & Dialogue System (Expanded)"* — *"Ported from Triple Triad: character-taunts.json (empty, rebuilt from scratch). NPCs have mood-based dialogue that changes based on relationship. Connects to: Character Mood, AI Citizens, Social Hub, Rumors, Economy."* A World Dashboard `npc_taunts` panel with an NPC list, a dialogue bubble, six action buttons (Talk · Compliment · Insult · Gift · Challenge · Gossip, plus **Flirt** for the two `flirt: true` NPCs) and a five-entry history.
- **OWNS:** `MOOD_STATES` (5 bands → colour/icon/min/max), **`NPCS` — a large hard-coded array of NPCs, each carrying `id`, `name`, `role`, `icon`, a starting `mood`, a `flirt` flag and a full five-band dialogue table (6 lines per band, ~30 lines per NPC)**, `selectedNPC`, `lastTaunt`, `dialogueHistory`, `giftAmount = 100`.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** `export function initNpcTaunts` + **`window.initNpcTaunts`**. The `#wd-npc_taunts` panel is the host; all six action buttons are bound with `addEventListener` inside `attachTauntsListeners`.
- **CALLS OUT:** **NOTHING. `var API_BASE = '/api';` IS DECLARED AND NEVER USED** — there is **no `fetch`, no `/api/` call and no WebSocket anywhere in the file**, despite the header claiming it *"Connects to: Character Mood, AI Citizens, Social Hub, Rumors, Economy."*
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THE HEADER CLAIMS FIVE INTEGRATIONS AND THE FILE HAS ZERO — the strongest instance of the fabricated-surface class in the sweep.** `API_BASE` is dead, and every one of the six verbs mutates **a local array element** and re-renders: `npc.mood = Math.min(100, npc.mood + 20)` (gift), `+ 10` (compliment), `- 15` (insult), `±15 / −5` (challenge), `+12` (flirt). **Mood is per-session memory that dies on reload**, and no server route is even named. (2) **THE CHALLENGE OUTCOME IS `Math.random() > 0.5` AND THE RESULT IS PRESENTED AS A WON MATCH** — *"You won! I'll get you next time!"* / *"Ha! Better luck next time, rookie."* with a real success/error toast, in a game whose match authority is server-side and deterministic. This is exactly the revision `.clinerules/app-entry-mandate.md` §8 removed from `pet_battle_arena.js` (*"Never re-introduce a client-side arena simulation — the revision replaced by this rule rolled dice with `Math.random` and paid fake $VBV"*), and the same defect recorded for `game_modes.js`. **The rule was obeyed in the file it named and not here.** (3) **THE GIFT IS PAID IN `SP`, AND `SP` IS NOT A LEDGER TOKEN.** The button reads `🎁 Gift (100 SP)` and the toast says `Gifted 100 SP to <npc>!` while the file sets `giftAmount = 100` and **nothing reads, checks or debits it**: the "gift" is a mood increment with a currency label attached, in a denomination appearing in no `$VBV`/`$VOI`/`$NUGGET`/`$UNIT` rail. `game_modes.js`'s casino used the same invented `SP`. (4) **THE GOSSIP LINES ARE EIGHT HARD-CODED "RUMORS" PRESENTED AS HEARD INFORMATION** — *"I saw the Warden taking bribes. Shh!"*, *"The Church is hiding something in the vault."*, *"They say the Casino is rigged… or is it?"* — while `/api/rumors` exists and is served (the sweep recorded `handlers_rumor.go` and `updateActiveRumors`): the panel invents rumors in a game that has a rumor system with its own feed. (5) **`Math.random()` PICKS EVERY LINE AT THREE SITES** — `renderDialogue`'s fallback, the Talk handler and the gossip/flirt arrays — so the same NPC at the same mood says something different on every render, **including on a re-render caused by an unrelated state change** (`renderNpcTaunts` is called by every handler, so clicking Insult can change the bubble text twice over). (6) **ALL SIX ACTIONS ARE UNGATED, UNCOOLED AND FREE** — no cooldown map, no `busy` lock, no cost, the buttons are not disabled during a re-render, so Insult can be spammed to mood 0 or Compliment to 100 with no limit, and `dialogueHistory` is capped at 20 (`if (dialogueHistory.length > 20) dialogueHistory.shift()`) so the record of a spam run is discarded. (7) **THE MOOD BANDS ARE DECLARED TWICE WITH DIFFERENT BOUNDARY SEMANTICS** — `MOOD_STATES` gives each band an inclusive `min`/`max` (Hostile 0-20, Annoyed 21-40, …) while `getMoodState(value)` uses `<=` chains (`≤ 20 … ≤ 40 … ≤ 60 … ≤ 80 … else Loyal`); they agree on integers but disagree conceptually (the table says Annoyed starts at 21, the function says anything above 20), and **`MOOD_STATES`' `min`/`max` are never read** — only `.color` — so the table's numbers are decoration beside the function that decides. (8) **`getMoodTrend` READS A FIELD THE HISTORY DOES CARRY** — `recent.moodValue > previous.moodValue`, and `addToHistory` **does** store `moodValue`, so the trend works; **but the history is capped at 20 across ALL NPCs**, so a trend for one NPC can be computed from two entries belonging to different conversations. (9) **Honest strengths:** the dialogue corpus is genuinely authored (each NPC has a distinct voice — Taya's tea house, Kay's arcade, Crypto Seraph's algorithm-prophecy — five bands × 6 lines each), all six buttons are `addEventListener`-bound with `selectedNPC` guards, the buttons render `disabled` when nothing is selected, and `renderNpcTaunts` interpolates only its own constants so no escaping is owed.
- **VERDICT:** **ambiguous → a fabricated-surface panel.** The authoring is real (a large, distinct, five-band dialogue corpus) but every verb is a **local mood mutation with no request**, a `Math.random()` challenge presented as a won match, a gift in a currency that does not exist, and eight invented "rumors" in a game that serves real ones — under a header claiming five integrations it does not have. The two rules it breaks are already written down: §8's *"never re-introduce a client-side arena simulation"* and the determinism mandate's treatment of dice.


### `Public/index.html` — 746 lines — THE SINGLE-ENTRY SHELL
- **PURPOSE:** ***the composition root's host page.*** The Single-Entry Mandate (`.clinerules/app-entry-mandate.md` §1) makes it *"a **pure shell**"* that *"may contain only: `wasm_exec.js` … third-party vendor bundles … the third-party WalletConnect modal ESM shim … `app.js` as `type="module"` … DOM markup"* — and §1's two prohibitions are explicit: *"Never add `<script src="js/...">` to `index.html`"* and *"Never add an inline `<script>` block with logic to `index.html`."*
- **ACQUISITION — THE FIVE ALLOWED THINGS, ALL PRESENT:** (1) **`wasm_exec.js`** as a classic script ✓; (2) `/vendor/algosdk.min.js` (`defer`) ✓; (3) `/vendor/walletconnect-sign-client.umd.js` (`defer`) ✓; (4) the **WalletConnect modal ESM shim** — an inline `<script type="module">` importing `/vendor/walletconnect-modal.mjs` and resolving the export under whatever alias the minifier chose (`WCM.WalletConnectModal || WCM.W || Object.values(WCM).find(v => typeof v === 'function' && v.name === 'WalletConnectModal')`), exactly the third-party shim §1 permits, with its reason in a comment; (5) **`<script src="app.js" type="module">`** ✓. **Plus two things §1 does not list:** `<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">` and — **`<script src="https://bundle.run/buffer@6.0.3"></script>` followed by an inline `<script>window.Buffer = window.Buffer || buffer.Buffer;</script>`**.
- **THE SHELL'S OWN RECORDED FIXES (each stated in place, which is why this file reads as a history of the refactor):** (a) the **FOUC guard** — `body { opacity: 0 }` + `body.ready { opacity: 1 }` with the reveal moved to `js/app_bridge.js`; (b) **`<meta name="walletconnect-project-id" content="INJECTED_VIA_SERVER_IDENTITY_MESSAGE">`** with *"This value is now dynamically injected via WebSocket identity message from the server, sourced from an environment variable"* — the env-only-secrets rule reaching the client config; (c) **no first-party `js/*.js` script tags at all** — the tail is a **list of comments where they were** (*"Justice Dashboard Module (PILLAR 7 …) — loaded as ES module via app.js import"* and the same for bonds, seasonal events, creator store, AI citizens, world events, leaderboard region, rivalry, life assets, early tasks, religion, faith, children bots, entity market, asset viewer, dev/game hub and web-3D), so the removal is documented rather than merely done; (d) **the admin container note** — *"The empty #admin-panel-overlay container was removed with admin_panel.js, which was its only user and which authenticated with a hard-coded password."*
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS (two live exceptions, one stale-comment residue):** (1) **~30 INLINE HANDLERS REMAIN AND ALL RESOLVE** — `connectWith(...)` ×3, `closeWalletSelector()`, `savePayoutAddress()`, `hideAllOverlays()` ×4, `setMasterVolume|setMusicVolume|setSfxVolume(this.value)`, `toggleMuteMaster|Music|Sfx()`, `toggleContextualAmbients()`, `closeSettingsOverlay()`, `applyAvatarFilters()` ×2, `switchShopCategory(...)` ×4, `adjustMapZoom(±0.1)` ×2, `fetchLeaderboard()`, `window.ToggleLeaderboard(); syncUI()`, `switchHofTab(...)` ×3, `filterSeasonHistory()`, `closeTournamentBracket()`, `proceedToWarRoom()`, `closeDeckManager()`, `window.AutoBuildDeck(); renderDeckManager()`, `addXChainWallet()` — **and the one that was broken in the previous session (the Deck Manager's Return button calling an unpublished `closeDeckManager()`) is now correct, because `deck.js` publishes it.** (2) **THE ADMIN SUITE'S CONTROLS ARE `data-admin-action` WITH ZERO INLINE HANDLERS** — the 2026-09-15 (b) conversion, visible here as `data-admin-action="simulate-mojo-decay"`, `"refresh-dlc"`, `"add-dlc-product"`, `"edit-presets"`, matching `admin_suite.js`'s ONE wiring table. (3) **THE TWO HONEST EXCEPTIONS TO §1:** the **`bundle.run` CDN script** (a remote third-party bundle rather than a pinned `/vendor/*` one — and it contradicts the self-hosting note the WalletConnect bundle carries: *"Self-hosted UMD bundles (no CDN / Tracking-Prevention dependency)"*), and the **creator-store container's `position: fixed; inset: 10%`** where §7's contained-overlay mandate specifies *"`position:fixed; inset:0; overflow:hidden`"* and every sibling root in this file uses `.overlay` or `inset:0`. (4) **Comment residue, not defects:** the Deck Manager's Return button carries *"Matches the previous bare `renderDeckManager()` call"* (a fix `deck.js` now records at its own site) and the loader comments' `PILLAR` numbering predates the module-graph consolidation — documentation that has outlived its subject.
- **VERDICT:** **owner — the Single-Entry shell, and its compliance is measurable rather than asserted:** five permitted acquisitions (four scripts plus the mandated third-party ESM shim), **zero first-party `js/*.js` script tags** with every removal documented at its former position, **zero inline `<script>` blocks carrying logic** beyond the one line the polyfill note implies, the FOUC guard and the admin-container removal both recorded in place, and all ~30 remaining inline handlers resolving to published globals. Its two exceptions are worth a decision rather than a fix: the `bundle.run` CDN load and the `inset:10%` creator-store root.


### `tools/archscan/views.js` — 748 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"Architecture View Definitions — Data-Driven. Each view is a function(g, data) that renders into an SVG group. Categories are derived from directory/filename prefixes — no hardcoded lists."* It renders `architecture.html` from the three data objects `scan.js` produces.
- **OWNS:** the view functions (`viewFull`, `viewWasm`, `viewJS`, `viewSCSS`, `viewAnalytics` and the five analytics sub-charts), the `CATEGORY_PREFIXES` table (25 entries), `groupModulesByCategory`, `groupBridgesByPrefix`, and **`renderHealthChart`**.
- **DATA INPUTS (globals, not parameters):** `MANIFEST_DATA`, `ANALYTICS_DATA`, `WIRED_DATA`, and a module-level **`svg`** — every view mutates shared state rather than receiving it.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THE HEALTH SCORE IS EXACTLY THE ARBITRARY COMPOSITE THE SWEEP PREDICTED — and its own docstring admits it.** *"Health is calculated from 4 factors: 1. Wired ratio … 2. Flow integrity … 3. Module connectedness: ES modules with at least 1 import or export. 4. Build tag violations … **Each factor contributes 25 points to the 100-point score.**"* **Four unlike measurements weighted equally by construction**, implemented literally: `wiredScore = Math.round(wiredRatio * 25)`, `integrityScore = Math.round(integrityRatio * 25)`, `connectednessScore = Math.round(connectednessRatio * 25)`, `violationScore = 25 − Math.min(25, violations * 5)`. (2) **FACTOR 4 INVERTS ITS OWN CLAIM AND A MISSING SECTION SCORES AS A PERFECT SECTION.** `violationScore = 25 - violationPenalty` means zero violations = 25 … and the lookup is **`summary.violations || 0`**, so a manifest section that is **missing entirely** reports `0 violations` and awards the full 25 — the composite treats absence of evidence as evidence of absence, in the factor named for the violations it is measuring. (3) **THE WIRED FACTOR IS `WIRED_DATA`, WHOSE WEAKNESS THE SWEEP ALREADY NAMED:** it is the `archscan/wired.js` census answering *"is this path MENTIONED anywhere?"* — the exact question session (d) proved insufficient (*"referenced is not reachable"*). So **25 % of a published "App Health Score" is a mention census**, and that number is what a reader will quote. (4) **THE FLOW-INTEGRITY FACTOR IS `scan.js`'s NAMING ARTEFACT** — `integrityRatio = flowIntegrity.integrityPercent / 100`, where that percentage counts a bridge function as incomplete purely because its Go implementation's name does not start with `Get|Set|Sync|Handle|Toggle` (recorded in `scan.js`'s entry). **Two of the four factors therefore measure conventions rather than health — 50 of the 100 points.** (5) **`CONNECTEDNESS` CANNOT DISTINGUISH A LIVE MODULE FROM A DEAD ONE** — `connectionCount > 0`, where `connectionCount = exports.length + imports.length + windowBindings.length` (`scan.js`), so **a module whose only feature is a `window.X = …` binding to nothing scores as fully connected** — satisfied by exactly the shape `verify_ui_handlers.js` exists to detect. (6) **THE NUMBER IS RENDERED WITH A COLOUR LADDER AND A VERDICT WORD** — `>= 80 '#34d399' : >= 50 '#fbbf24' : '#fb7185'` and `'Healthy' | 'Needs Attention' | 'Critical'` — so a composite of two conventions and one mention census is presented as a clinical verdict, in a **generated artefact** the manifest note says is not tracked. (7) **`svg` IS A MODULE-LEVEL GLOBAL EVERY VIEW WRITES TO** — `svg.setAttribute('viewBox', …)` and `svg.innerHTML = ''` inside **both** `renderAnalyticsSub` and `renderOverviewChart`, so `renderOverviewChart` clears and rebuilds the SVG the caller just built: a leftover of a refactor that moved the clearing up a level. (8) **`groupBridgesByPrefix` HAS A 70-ALTERNATIVE REGEX ENDING IN PROJECT-SPECIFIC NAMES** — `(Get|Set|Sync|…|Calculate|Format|Parse|Esc|Fmt|Career|GetActive|MyClub|SendChallenge|Challenge|OpenRivalry)` — where the last five are whole project names appended after the generic verbs, and `GetActive`/`OpenRivalry` **can never match anyway** because `Get` and `Open` appear earlier in the alternation. A category table grown by appending reached this state. (9) **`CATEGORY_PREFIXES` DUPLICATES `scan.js`'s `deriveModuleCategory` TABLE** — 25 entries here, 5 grouped rules there — and `groupModulesByCategory` prefers `mod.category` (set by the scanner) **falling back to the local `getCategory`**, so two tables coexist and can disagree about a module the scanner did not categorise. (10) **Honest strengths:** the views are genuinely data-driven (`` `${jsModules.length} Modules (${MANIFEST_DATA.summary.esModules} ES)` `` reads the manifest rather than typing a number), every optional section is guarded (`MANIFEST_DATA.scssPartials || []`), `makePie`/`makeRect`/`makeLine`/`makeText`/`addNode` are real SVG builders, and the breakdown panel prints **all four components with their own numerators** — so a reader who scrolls past the number can see how it was made.
- **VERDICT:** ambiguous → **a generated-report renderer whose headline number is a composite of four equally-weighted unlike measurements, two of which measure naming conventions and one a mention census**, with a missing manifest section scoring as a perfect section in the violations factor. The breakdown beneath the score is honest; the score above it is not.


### `Public/js/game.js` — 924 lines
- **PURPOSE:** no header block — **the match client**: the board, the challenge lifecycle, the lobby player list, chat, match history, deck rating, the power tooltip, quick-cast, the spectator wager and warm-boot rejoin. It imports `showToast`, `hideAllOverlays`, `showMatchPreview`, `renderCardHTML`, `movePowerTooltip`, `hidePowerTooltip`, `showQuickCastMenu`, `handleLocalBanUI`, `tooltipEl` from `ui.js`, `socket`/`myClientId` from `network.js`, `collectiveIntelligence`, and `initAudioContext`.
- **OWNS:** `activeCardId`, `aiThinking`, `pendingQuickCastId`, `lastBoardState`, `currentChallengerId`, `currentOpponentId`, `spectatorMatchState`, `myPlayerIndex`, `matchHistorySaved`, `lastLobbyPlayers`, `lastTauntPhase`, `lastTauntTurn` — with **nine exported setters** as the only writers for other modules.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** ~28 ESM exports + **`window.rejoinActiveMatch`, `window.openSpectatorWagerOverlay`, `window.submitSpectatorWager`** (the last two with the in-place fix note: *"Two globals this module's OWN rendered markup names: the PLACE WAGER button in the spectator HUD and the wager form's submit. Both functions live here, and an inline handler resolves its name on `window` — so both controls were inert until they were published."*) + `window.refreshIdentity`.
- **CALLS OUT:** the WS types `join_queue` / `leave_queue` / `chat` / `challenge` (invite|accept|decline|sync_back) / `move` / `spectate` / `use_item` / `refresh_identity`; **`POST /api/match/wager`**; ~25 WASM bridge globals (`GetGameState`, `PlaceCard`, `ApplyArtifactToBoard`, `StartMatch`, `ForceActive`, `SetBoardState`, `ResetGame`, `syncUI`, `SetInMatchmakingQueue`, `GetLevelLabelForDisplay`, `InitiateRecovery`, `PlaySelectSound`, `toggleNetwork`).
- **DOM/HOST:** `#board-container`, `#btn-matchmaking`, `#pp-lobby-players` (with `#active-players` fallback), `#chat-input`, `#chat-display`, `#history-display`, `#challenge-overlay`/`#challenge-text`, `#match-preview-overlay`, `#spectator-wager-overlay`, `.power-tooltip`.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **A LIVE `ReferenceError` THAT HAS NEVER THROWN — a cut-and-paste corruption at FOUR sites.** `toggleMatchmakingQueue`, `proceedToWarRoom`, `sendChallenge` and one more each contain the literal **`initwindow.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext();`** where an `initAudioContext()` call belongs: `initwindow` is **undefined**, so the statement throws — unreached only because each site sits after an earlier guard (`!userAddress`, `spectatorMatchState`, socket OPEN). **The audio-context initialisation at all four sites is dead**, the statement is a landmine on the first path that reaches it, and the top-level `import { initAudioContext } from './audio.js'` is therefore **imported and never used** — evidence the intended call was mangled into this text. (2) **`acceptChallenge` SHOWS A "DECLINED" TOAST ON SUCCESS — a real, always-firing wrong message.** It sends the `accept` envelope, then `showToast(`❌ Challenge from ${currentChallengerId} declined.`, "info")` under *"PILLAR 5: Visual Confirmation. Provide explicit UI feedback that the challenge has been rejected."* — the comment and the message agree with each other and both contradict the function name. Same polarity class as `game_multiplayer.js`'s inverted win test. (3) **`activeCardId = null` IS WRITTEN TWICE IN `clickGrid` WITH AN IDENTICAL COMMENT** once before the multiplayer broadcast and once after: idempotent, but a merge leftover — and the **first** null happens before the card lookup (`(state.deck || []).find(c => c.id === parseInt(selectedCardId))` survives only because `selectedCardId` was captured first), so a future reorder breaks the power lookup silently. (4) **`renderChatMessage` INTERPOLATES PEER-AUTHORED TEXT INTO `innerHTML` UNESCAPED** — `msgDiv.innerHTML = `<b>${sender}:</b> ${text}`` where `text` is a chat message relayed from **another player** and `sender` is raw too. The same injection path recorded for `game_multiplayer.js`, in the busier surface; the typewriter branch is safe (`content.textContent += …`), the ordinary branch is not. (5) **THE CHAT CAP IS A REAL, DOCUMENTED FIX WHOSE COMMENT CARRIES THE MEASUREMENT** — *"PERFORMANCE HARD GUARD: bound the chat DOM. The server can broadcast a very high rate of chat messages (autonomous NPC/audit chatter); without a cap the `#chat-display` list grows without limit, forcing a full-document style/layout recalculation on every append and freezing the UI in multi-second jumps."* — `MAX_CHAT_NODES = 120` plus a `while` trim. The 2026-09-13 lag fix, in place. (6) **THE 2 % HOUSE CUT IS COMPUTED IN THE CLIENT ON FLOATS** — `const potentialPayout = wager * (1 - 0.02)` inside `window.updatePotentialPayout`, itself **assigned as a global from inside the overlay builder** and named by the input's inline `oninput`. Display-only, but the figure shown before committing money comes from a rate the server owns; `submitSpectatorWager` does the authoritative part correctly (`Math.round(wagerAmount * 1000000)` to micro). (7) **`submitSpectatorWager` GATES ON `state.virtual_balance < wagerAmount`** — a float balance against a float wager — while the same function converts to micro for the request: two representations of one money value. (8) **`showPowerTooltip` DERIVES `let reduction = ownerNurturing` AND REASSIGNS IT** (`if (reduction > baseFatiguePenalty) { reduction = baseFatiguePenalty; }`) — correct, and the reassignment is the class the mandate prefers expressed arithmetically. (9) **`updatePlayerList` INTERPOLATES `p.id` INTO INLINE HANDLERS** — `onclick="sendChallenge('${p.id}')"` / `onclick="sendSpectate('${p.id}')"` — the lobby payload's client id, unescaped, in a single-quoted JS string inside a double-quoted attribute. (10) **Honest strengths:** `clickGrid` **guards the WASM bridge before any IPC**, checks `replay_state !== "SYNCHRONIZED"`, checks the turn against `state.local_player_index` and checks `activeCardId === null` **before** placing — four ordered refusals each with its own toast; `renderMatchHistory` prefers **server-authoritative history** (`me.match_history`, with `receipt_txid` labelled *"Sync with authoritative common_types.go JSON tag"*) over localStorage, has a real `isRenderingHistory` re-entrancy guard, and **batch-resolves all opponent names in one `Promise.all`**; `calculateDeckRating` is integer bin arithmetic with explicit clamping; `pendingQuickCastId` prevents the quick-cast double-fire; and `rejoinActiveMatch` reads a `vbabes_state_beacon` and forces recovery on a **hash mismatch** rather than trusting the cache.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the match client) — the client's busiest module, carrying the chat cap fix, the pre-IPC bridge guards, server-authoritative history and the beacon hash check; its defects are a **mangled `initwindow.AudioContext` statement at four sites that silently killed audio initialisation and would throw on the first path reaching it**, an **`acceptChallenge` that toasts "declined"**, **unescaped peer chat into `innerHTML`**, and a duplicated `activeCardId = null` masking an ordering dependency.



### `Public/prototypes/nexus-v2.html` — 932 lines — PROTOTYPE (un-composed; excluded from the module walk by design)
- **PURPOSE:** *"NFT-Seduction | Nexus Hub — Living Grimoire"* — a **standalone design prototype** of the constellation hub: a full-viewport `.nexus-shell` (`position:fixed; inset:0; overflow:hidden` — §7's contained contract), a star/nebula parallax background, a `#particle-canvas`, a top bar with wallet + theme + climate, a region preview, the feature-node constellation with zoom, and four control buttons. Its `<style>` block is self-contained (~500 lines) and carries the design-token set (`--neon-cyan`, `--arena-mood-color`, `--tone-mood`) the compiled SCSS later adopted.
- **WHY IT IS IN THE SWEEP AT ALL:** `verify_module_reachability.js` excludes it via `SKIP_DIR = /…(vendor|node_modules|**prototypes**|Assets|Generated|devdata|\.git)…/i`, and **nothing names it** — a search of `index.html`, `app.js` and the gate itself for `nexus-v2` returns **zero hits**. It is an un-composed prototype by the tree's own rules, recorded as such rather than counted as a page. `verify_ui_handlers.js` shares the same SKIP set, so its eight inline handlers (`toggle3DWorld()`, `zoom(±0.1)`, `resetZoom()`, `simulateUnlock()`, `highlightPath()`, `toggleParticles()`, `resetDemo()`) are outside that gate too.
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS / WHAT IT TEACHES:** (1) **IT IS THE ONLY SURFACE IN THE SWEEP THAT DISTINGUISHES MOCK DATA FROM LIVE DATA HONESTLY — with a flag, a toast and a console line.** The data layer opens *"=== DATA LAYER: Live endpoint with mock fallback ==="* with `const mockData = {…}` commented *"Mock matches /api/player/progression response for empty wallet"*; `fetchProgression()` tries **the real endpoint** (`await fetch('/api/player/progression')`, `if (!resp.ok) throw`), and on success sets `isLiveData = true` and toasts **`'Live data connected — ThemeEngine active'`**; the catch does `console.warn('Using mock data — endpoint not reachable:', err.message); gameData = mockData; isLiveData = false;`. **That is the opposite of `remaining_tabs.js`, `npc_taunts.js` and `faith_church.js`:** the fallback is *labelled* at both boundaries and the reader is told which one they are seeing. (2) **THE MOCK CARRIES A COHERENT STATE MODEL** — a wallet, `theme: {tone, element, intensity, entropy, mood_tag}`, `region: {name: "Governor", climate: "BLIGHTED", disaster_tier: 3}`, **sixteen features each with `state: alive|dawning|dormant`, a `progress` and a `gate_text`** (`clubs: '5000 VBV to found'`, `governor: 'Own 2 territories'`, `regional: 'Become Governor first'`) and **seven `constellation_paths`** — demonstrating the unlock-gate vocabulary the real career/civil-rank system later implemented. One invented value persists: the region is named **`Governor`**, the same sample-data artefact recorded for `remaining_tabs.js`'s `initRegions` and `territory_map.js`. (3) **A REAL LEAK IN THE PARTICLE LOOP** — `animateParticles` returns early when disabled (so it stops correctly), **but `toggleParticles` restarts it by calling `animateParticles()` without cancelling a pending frame**, and the initial load-time call plus a toggle can leave two rAF chains drawing the same canvas; `animationId` holds only the last handle. (4) **`celebrateNPCs()` SWAPS VIDEO SOURCES FROM A STALE `.src` AND NEVER CLEARS ITS TIMER** — `const base = currentSrc.replace('-idle.mp4', '')`, then `video.src = base + '-celebrate.mp4'` with a 3-second `setTimeout` restoring `-idle`: two rapid unlocks can restore `-idle` over a `-celebrate` in flight. (5) **`highlightPath()` AND `simulateUnlock()` PICK WITH `Math.random()`** — presentation-only in a prototype, and each of the seven paths is a *real* declared progression chain, so the random choice is over authored data rather than invented. (6) **The `[data-tone]`/`[data-element]` selectors MUTATE `gameData.theme` IN PLACE**, including when `gameData` is the fetched live object — a local edit of a read-model, correct for a design tool and worth noting only because the same file fetched that object from a real route. (7) **`toggle3DWorld()` IS A TOAST** — `showToast('3D World: Camera fly-through activated', 'info')` — while the composed `world3d.js` now provides a real `enter3DWorld`: the pre-implementation placeholder, honestly one line long. (8) **Eight inline handlers, all defined in this file's own inline `<script>`** — compliant for a page that is *its own* composition root (the reachability gate's page-declared rule), which is exactly why the handler gate's SKIP set matters: these names are page-local, not app globals.
- **VERDICT:** **prototype, un-composed by measurement** (`SKIP_DIR` plus zero references from `index.html`, `app.js` or the gates) — and worth keeping precisely because it is the **counter-example to the fabricated-surface class**: its mock data is labelled at the fetch boundary, flagged with `isLiveData`, announced in a toast and named in a console warning, and its state vocabulary (16 features × `alive|dawning|dormant` × a `gate_text`, plus 7 authored progression paths) is the model the composed hub later adopted.


### `Public/js/bonded_branding.js` — 1012 lines
- **PURPOSE:** ***"bonded_branding.js — §23.5 BONDED BRANDING STUDIO (ecosphere-wide theming)"*** — *"Bonded assets are the player's own art. This is where a player paints an asset and wears it on ANY entity they own: items, themes, bots, pets, vehicles, churches, clubs, shops, world content — anything an image can be tied to, for branding. **CARDS ARE EXCLUDED** … The client does not decide that: the server refuses card kinds, refuses to enumerate them, and serves the blocked list in `policy.blocked_target_kinds`. **This module RENDERS the served policy rather than re-declaring it.**"* The header names all six routes it uses.
- **OWNS:** `bbState` (policy, assets, bindings, targets, kindFilter, capacity, `cardView`/`cardViewPolicy`, `market`/`marketError`, `busy`), `bbShop`/`bbShopPrice`, and every §10.6/§10.7/§10.8 surface the studio renders: mint, targets, **card eyes**, theme slots, app slides, the placeholder-pack shop and the player-to-player market.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** ~24 `window.*` bindings — `openBondedBranding`, `initBondedBranding`, `bbMint`, `bbBind`, `bbUnbind`, `bbFilterKind`, `bbCvsApply`, `bbCvsClear`, `bbSlideApply`, `bbSlideClear`, `bbClaimStarter`, `bbBuySku`, `bbRenderSlides`, `bbThemeBind`, `bbThemeLock`, **`bbThemeUnlock`**, `bbRenderThemeSlots`, `bbLoadMarket`, `bbListItem`, `bbCancelListing`, `bbBuyListing` — plus the ESM openers, with the navigation contract in place: *"Reached ONLY from the World Dashboard (§5 two-tier navigation). initBondedBranding exists as the embed fallback the dashboard uses when the standalone opener is unavailable."*
- **CALLS OUT:** **`GET /api/assets`**, **`GET /api/assets/targets`**, **`POST /api/assets/mint|bind|unbind`**, **`GET /api/assets/branding`** (public read), **`GET|POST /api/assets/card-view`**, **`GET /api/assets/catalogue`**, **`POST /api/assets/starter`**, the **§10.8 market** routes, **`POST /api/theme/bind|lock`**, and `window.SlideTheming`/`window.CardViewSkins` for the two viewer-scoped layers.

- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** **none material — this is the sweep's most carefully-built module, and its care is documented rather than implied.** Named evidence: (1) **`bbParseVbvMicro` CONVERTS TYPED MONEY WITH NO FLOAT AT ALL, AND SAYS WHY** — *"turns a typed '$VBV' amount into micro units, exactly: the string is parsed as digits plus at most six decimal places, so '12.5' is 12_500_000 micro with no float anywhere. Returns null when the text is not money."* — one anchored regex plus `whole * 1000000 + frac`: the correct integer-boundary pattern. (2) **`bbThemeLockToggle` REFUSES TO FAKE AN UNLOCK — the honest-refusal model.** *"`locked` is the ONLY thing this route sets — there is no 'unlock' route, so an unlock is stated as unavailable rather than faked by a client-side flag."* — and the code matches: `if (!locked) { bbThemeStatus('The engine exposes lock only; a locked binding is not unlocked by any served route.', true); return; }`. **The Unlock button exists, is published, and reports the engine's own limitation** rather than toggling a local boolean. (3) **THE SLOT-KEY RULE IS STATED, VALIDATED AND EXPLAINED** — *"A theme slot binding is keyed `<asset>:<slot>` … **The slot label may not contain ':' — that key shape belongs to an entity target binding.**"* — enforced at the door (`if (slot.indexOf(':') >= 0)`) and repeated in the rendered rule text. (4) **PER-CALL FAULT TOLERANCE WITH A NAMED PROBLEMS LIST** — `bbLoad` reads assets, targets and card-view in three independent `try` blocks pushing into `problems[]`, then reports *"Partly unreadable — …"*; **one refused read never blanks the others**, and the no-wallet branch still reads the PUBLIC policy so *"a visitor can see the rules (and that cards are excluded) instead of staring at an unexplained empty studio."* (5) **THE RATE-LIMIT RULE IS IMPLEMENTED WITH ITS MANDATE CITED** — *"a refused read is retried once; if it is still refused the panel SAYS so rather than rendering 'you own nothing' (app-entry-mandate §3)"* — and `bbApi` throws the distinctive **`'rate-limited — could not be read; try again shortly'`**. (6) **THE CAPACITY IS SERVED, NEVER INFERRED, AND ITS ZERO CASE IS EXPLAINED IN THE RENDER** — *"The chest serves the wallet's own creation budget (§23.5.1) — never inferred client-side"*, plus `` `Bonded assets: ${used}/${limit} — capacity equals your card/deck NFT supply.${limit === 0 ? ' You hold no card/deck NFTs yet, so you cannot create one.' : ''}` ``. (7) **THE MINT FORM VALIDATES THE SERVER'S OWN CONTRACT BEFORE SENDING** — a name, a URI, **`/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i` for the sha256**, a positive byte size, each with its own message, and the byte/dimension inputs carry `max="${limits.max_bytes}"` / `max_dimension` **read from the served media policy**. (8) **STALE MARKET LISTINGS ARE SHOWN UNBUYABLE WITH THE SERVER'S REASON** — `if (status === 'active' && !row.stale_reason)` gates Buy/Cancel and `row.stale_reason` renders as `` `cannot be bought: ${reason}` ``. (9) **THE MARKET RULE IS RENDERED FROM THE SERVED PAYLOAD** — `` `The house takes ${fee} bps of the price and the rest goes to the seller. ${view.acquisition_rule}` `` — including the §23.5.1 acquisition exemption, with the header stating *"this client never re-declares a price or a policy."* (10) **`bbSafeUri` DOES NOT INVENT A GATEWAY** — `https|http|ipfs|ar` admitted, everything else `''`: *"Only schemes the server accepts are renderable; anything else is stated, never loaded."* (11) **EVERY MUTATING VERB IS `busy`-LOCKED** (`bbMint`/`bbBind`/`bbUnbind` all `if (bbState.busy) return; … finally { bbState.busy = false; }`) and every refusal names what was refused (`'Mint refused: '`, `'Binding refused: '`, `'Unbind refused: '`, `'Card eyes refused: '`).
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the §23.5 studio and the §10.6/§10.7/§10.8 theming surfaces) — **the sweep's model module**: an integer-only money parser at the boundary, an unlock that reports the engine's limitation instead of faking it, a slot-key rule stated and validated at the door, three independent fault-tolerant reads with a named problems list, a served capacity whose zero case is explained, a mint form enforcing the server's own media contract, and stale listings that explain why they cannot be bought.


### `Public/js/menu_customization.js` — 1013 lines
- **PURPOSE:** *"menu_customization.js — Button shapes, sizes, grid layouts, and controller nav"* — *"60+ button shapes, 6 size tiers, 9 grid types, per-button overrides. Controller-friendly: each grid type maps to a navigation model."* Seven numbered sections: the shape library · sizes · grids · per-system and per-pathway shape maps · controller navigation · the public API.
- **OWNS:** **`SHAPES`** (~60 entries, each `{name, icon, clip, hitDirs, desc}`) · **`SIZES`** (6 tiers) · **`GRIDS`** (9 types, each owning its own `compute` function) · **`PATHWAY_SHAPES`** and **`SYSTEM_SHAPES`** (a per-system icon vocabulary: `items → pill`, `mutation → syringe`, `clubs → campfire`, `dlc → key`, `localmodel → brain`, `church → church`, `npc → sparkles`, …) · **`CONTROLLER_MAP`** (10 grid types → a direction vocabulary) · **`RADIAL_GRIDS`** and **`FLOW_GRIDS`**.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** a 20-name ESM export (`SHAPES`, `SIZES`, `GRIDS`, `RADIAL_GRIDS`, `FLOW_GRIDS`, `PATHWAY_SHAPES`, `SYSTEM_SHAPES`, `CONTROLLER_MAP`, `getShapeForSystem`, `getPathwayShape`, `getSize`, `getGrid`, `computePositions`, `getClipPath`, `getControllerNav`, `getAllShapeIds`, `getAllGridIds`, `getAllSizeIds`, `isRadialGrid`, `isPositionedGrid`). **No `window.` bindings** — a pure library, consumed by `menu-constellation.js`, `menu_customization_panel.js`, `controller_nav.js` and the constellation hub.
- **CALLS OUT:** **nothing** — no fetch, no `/api/`, no DOM, no globals. Pure data plus pure functions (the grid `compute` callbacks are the only behaviour).
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** **none material — and two of the sweep's recurring defect CLASSES were fixed here, with the reasoning recorded in place:** (1) **`FLOW_GRIDS` IS THE ONE OWNER OF THE IDS TWO CONSUMERS MIS-SPELLED** — *"Grids that lay items out in FLOW (no absolute coordinates). ONE owner for this too: both the panel and the constellation tested `['grid','linear-h','linear-v']` — **ids that do not exist (the real keys are `linearH`/`linearV`)** — so those two layouts were painted with absolute positioning they do not use."* — and `isPositionedGrid` is the derived predicate every consumer now calls. **`controller_nav.js` is the remaining consumer still carrying the dead spellings**, which is why that finding lives in its own entry rather than here. (2) **`RADIAL_GRIDS` IS THE SAME FIX FOR A MISSING CONTROL** — *"Grids that place items on a ring around a centre. ONE owner for this list: the customization panel used to spell `['circle','arc']` inline, so a new radial grid would silently lose its Radius control."* — the `spokes` grid is the case that proved it. (3) **The shape library is a genuine authored design system** — ~60 shapes, each with a `clip-path`, a **hit-direction declaration** (`hitDirs: ['left','right']` for `oval`, `['up','down']` for `star`, all four for `hexagon`/`octagon`/`map`/`globe`) and a **pathway/system mapping written in prose** (`'Tactical/industrial — P-Justice, P-AOS pathways'`, `'Lockdown/bonds — P-Lockdown pathway exclusive'`) — so a shape's navigation model and its narrative owner are both declared rather than inferred. (4) **`CONTROLLER_MAP` DECLARES TEN MODELS, FOUR OF WHICH ARE NOT DIRECTIONS** — `circle`/`spokes` → `center`/`outer`/`cw`/`ccw`, `triangle` → `prev-layer`/`next-layer`/`sibling-prev`/`sibling-next`, `freeform` → `tab-prev`/`tab-next` — a **navigation SEMANTICS table**, not a delta table, which is the right shape for a library whose consumer should interpret them. **`controller_nav.js` interprets none of them**: it switches on the grid type itself and re-implements `moveFocus`. (5) **`SYSTEM_SHAPES` NAMES TWO ENTRIES THE PRODUCT DOES NOT HAVE AS SHAPES** — `dlc: 'key'` (DLC exists as an admin surface only) and `localmodel: 'brain'` (a promotion registry): harmless defaults for a lookup, noted only because the map is otherwise a precise inventory of real features. (6) **`getClipPath`, `getSize` AND `getGrid` ALL FALL BACK** (`SHAPES.circle.clip`, `SIZES.md`, `GRIDS.grid`) rather than throwing, so an unknown id renders a valid button instead of an unstyled one — the correct failure direction for a presentation library. (7) **A structural note, not a defect:** ~900 of the 1013 lines are declaration, and `computePositions` delegates to `GRIDS[type].compute`, so the nine layout algorithms live inside the table — cohesive, but it means the file is mostly vocabulary rather than logic.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the shape/size/grid/controller vocabulary) — **a clean library and the only file where BOTH of the sweep's recurring id classes were fixed with the reason preserved**: one owner for the radial list (which had silently withheld a Radius control) and one for the flow list (which had been painted with coordinates it does not use), plus ~60 authored shapes each declaring its hit directions and its narrative owner.

### `Public/app.js` — 1386 lines — THE COMPOSITION ROOT
- **PURPOSE:** *"PILLAR 5: Modular Orchestration. app.js acts as the central hub, importing authoritative domain logic and exposing it to the global window scope for index.html accessibility."* It carries **~180 imports** (every first-party module) and **~250 `window.*` bindings**, and it owns `window.onload` — the WASM boot.
- **OWNS:** the composition graph itself (the Single-Entry Mandate's ONE root), the boot sequence, **`window.syncUI`** (the app's single render orchestrator), `window.UserPreferences` (a 31-key facade over the ESM store), `window.onload`, and ~20 HUD updaters.
- **THE IMPORT BLOCK IS ITS OWN DOCUMENTED HISTORY — three comments carry the refactor:** (1) *"UI MODULE IMPORTS — SINGLE-ENTRY MANDATE. index.html is a PURE SHELL: wasm_exec.js + third-party vendor bundles + app.js. Every first-party script is imported HERE so there is exactly ONE composition root and ONE boot order, with wasm_exec as the glue. **These were previously `<script src="js/*.js">` tags inside index.html, which caused every module to be evaluated twice (once classic, once as a module) and produced two competing UI stacks** — the World Dashboard and the Player Profile hub behaving like separate apps. Every file below is a self-contained IIFE that binds its public API to window, so import order is not load-bearing **beyond app_bridge.js (which must define window.WasmWalletBridge before the WASM engine calls into JS)**."* (2) **the orphan-cleaner note** — *"The module existed on disk but was never composed into the app, so that route was DEAD: the dashboard's typeof-guard silently fell back to embedding `initOrphans` and the intended surface was unreachable."* (3) **the admin note** — *"The admin surface: ONE signature-gated console … The four competing dashboards (admin_dashboard / operations_dashboard / final_dashboard / admin_panel) were deleted — they were never mounted, never called, and one of them authenticated with a hard-coded password"*, plus the suite's **eight-dead-controls** record (*"eight of those functions had no publisher, so those controls were inert. The markup now declares `data-admin-action` and this module binds them."*).
- **PURPOSE-BEARING COMMENTS ON SINGLE IMPORTS (each is a rule, not decoration):** `theme_engine.js` — *"_theme_engine.scss + _variables.scss already consume those tokens, so until this import existed the CSS contract was INERT. Default element is 'fire', which is exactly the token default the compiled :root already ships — so composing it changes nothing until setElement() is called."* · `tx_journal.js` — *"memo of this browser's OWN transactions; pending is never shown as settled"* · `faction_shop.js` — *"owner of /api/faction/shop + /api/faction/shop/buy, which had no UI anywhere in the client. Placed as a Careers & Factions leaf because the engine gates buying on the caller's career role."*

- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **A REAL DEFECT IN THE BOOT PATH: THE WHOLE BOOT SITS INSIDE ONE `try`, SO ANY POST-`go.run` FAILURE IS REPORTED AS AN ENGINE FAILURE AND THE UI NEVER STARTS.** `window.onload = async () => { console.log("[ARENA] Initiating Neural Uplink..."); const go = new Go(); try { await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(fetch("main.wasm"), go.importObject); go.run(result.instance); renderGameScreen(); bindAdminSuiteControls(); … beacon restore … initWebSocket(handleServerMessage); initParticleSystem(); buildEmptyBoard(); setInterval(sendPing, 30000); window.syncUI(); rejoinActiveMatch(); } catch (err) { console.error("[BOOT ERROR] Engine initialization failed:", err); showToast("❌ Critical Error: Neural Uplink Failed. Please refresh.", "error", 0); } }` — **the catch names an ENGINE failure for every step**, and because the WebSocket, `syncUI` and the heartbeat are all inside the same block, a throw from `bindAdminSuiteControls()`, from a malformed beacon (which has its own inner `try`, so it is the exception that proves the rule) or from any HUD updater leaves **a live WASM engine with no network and no rendered UI**. (2) **`window.onload` IS ASSIGNED AS A PROPERTY, NOT AN EVENT LISTENER** — with `app.js` as `type="module"` the module's tail runs before `load` fires, so this works today; but any second assignment anywhere would **silently replace** this one. `addEventListener('load', …)` is the shape that cannot be clobbered. (3) **THE ROOT COMPOSES TWO MODULES WHOSE SURFACES THE HANDLER CENSUS SKIPS** — `./js/npc_taunts.js` and `./js/game_multiplayer.js` are imported here, which is what makes their panels reachable and their fabricated-surface findings (recorded in their own entries) **live rather than latent**. (4) **`window.initMatchArena = window.openMatchArena || function () {};` IS A SILENT NO-OP FALLBACK** — if the real opener is absent, the WD's `match_arena` tab resolves to an empty function **with no report**, unlike the dashboard's usual "not wired yet" placeholder. (5) **`window.syncUI`'s REDUNDANT-RENDER GUARD READS INVERTED** — `if (scope !== "combat" && scope !== "solvency_override" && currentStateKey === dashboardCache.stateKey && state.faucet === dashboardCache.lastBalance) { if (scope !== "all") return; }` — for `scope === "all"` the guard **falls through and renders anyway** while every narrower scope returns early. Deliberate (the key is computed per-scope) but the nesting reads as a bug, and `state.faucet` is used as the balance in a key otherwise built from twelve other fields. (6) **A RELATIVE FETCH AND AN ORDER RULE WORTH RECORDING** — `fetch("main.wasm")` resolves against the document (`/main.wasm`), correct for the shipped layout; and the beacon restore is explicitly ordered (player index → profile → sequence → phase → board → balances) with the reason in place: *"Must restore player index before syncing profile to ensure correct slot hydration."* (7) **Honest strengths:** the import block is **exhaustively commented with a reason for each risky import**, including the one load-bearing order dependency (`app_bridge.js` first among the IIFEs); `syncUI` has a **real delta-safe guard** (`if (liquidEl && totalLiquid !== null)`), a **granular node-diff that preserves the `game.js`-attached `.onclick` listeners** (*"Update individual grid slots to preserve the .onclick listeners established in game.js:buildEmptyBoard"*), an explicit owner/rarity class mapping, the board-visibility rule stated as an operator mandate (*"the game board must ONLY show during an Active match, a live spectate session, or replay catch-up"*), and a phase→audio-context bridge that names its own source (`transitionToContext(contextKey, 'syncUI')`).
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the composition graph and the boot) — **the Single-Entry Mandate's one root, and the file whose comments are the codebase's history of the refactor**: ~180 imports with a stated reason on each risky one, ~250 publications, the WASM boot with a beacon warm-start in a deliberate order, and `syncUI` as the one render orchestrator with a delta guard and listener-preserving grid diffing — **its one live defect is a single `try` around the whole boot, so any post-`go.run` failure is reported as an engine failure and the WebSocket and UI never start.**



### `Public/js/ui.js` — 1533 lines
- **PURPOSE:** no header block — **the presentation layer**: ~40 exported renderers, updaters and HUDs, and **the ONE owner of two cross-cutting contracts** (overlay closing and toast dispatch). It imports from `particles.js`, `network.js`, `wallet.js`, `game.js`, `audio.js`, `admin.js`, `criminality.js`, `leaderboard.js`, `utils.js` and `economy.js` — the broadest import fan-in in the client.

- **ENTRY POINTS:** ~40 ESM exports + **`window.showToast`, `window.highlightStartButton`, `window.toggleActionDropdown`** and the three that were dead until published — with the reason in place: *"Every handler name this module's OWN rendered markup uses must exist on `window` — an inline handler resolves its name there — but these are module functions, so each control was inert: `openRegionalManager` — the territory view's 'OPEN REGIONAL MANAGER ABILITY' button; `showQuickCastMenu` — the board tooltip's 'QUICK-CAST ITEM' button; `closeSettingsOverlay` — the settings overlay's CLOSE button."*
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **`hideAllOverlays` IS THE DOCUMENTED OWNER OF THE TWO-CONTRACT RULE — the clearest statement of §7 in the tree:** *"TWO CLOSE CONTRACTS — and they must not be mixed. Legacy `.overlay` panels close with the `.hidden` CLASS. `.vbt-overlay` panels and `.pp-hub` close with INLINE display, because that is how their openers reveal them. `.hidden` is defined as `display: none !important` (_spacing.scss, _faucet_dashboard.scss). Adding `.hidden` to an inline-contract root therefore **BEATS the `style.display = 'flex'` its opener sets, leaving the panel rendered but permanently invisible (`computed: none`)**. That is why roots carrying BOTH `.overlay` and `.vbt-overlay` must be closed inline."* — implemented as one pass over `.overlay` branching on `inlineContract`, **plus a second pass over `.vbt-overlay, .pp-hub`** to cover roots that do not also carry `.overlay`. (2) **`showToast` HAS TWO COMPETING FADE TIMERS, AND THE `critical` DURATION IS APPLIED TO ONLY ONE.** The toast is first scheduled by `setTimeout(() => { toast.classList.add("toast-fade-out"); setTimeout(() => toast.remove(), 300); }, duration)`, and then, at the very end, by a **second** `if (duration > 0) { setTimeout(() => { toast.style.opacity = '0'; toast.style.transform = 'translateX(100%)'; toast.style.transition = '0.5s'; setTimeout(() => toast.remove(), 500); }, duration); }` on the same element. The `type === "critical"` line reassigns `duration = 8000` **after** the first timer was already armed with the original value — so the class-based fade fires at the old duration and only the inline animation honours the extension. Both mechanisms are live and neither knows about the other. (3) **THE PARTICLE/SFX LADDER DISPATCHES BY SUBSTRING-MATCHING THE MESSAGE TEXT** — eighteen `message.includes(...)` tests keyed on literals like `"KIDNAP GAMBIT"`, `"MUTATION FAILURE"`, `"TERRITORY INVASION"`, `"CLOAK DISRUPTED"`, `"CONTRACT COMPLETED"`, `"REPARATION RECEIVED"` — so **a presentation layer is coupled to the exact wording of server-authored text**: reword a message anywhere and its effect silently disappears, and the `else { triggerGlobalKidnapEffect(); }` **fallback fires a specific visual effect for any unmatched `critical`** rather than none. (4) **`updateSpectatorHUD` WRITES AN INVALID DECLARATION INLINE** — `style="… border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.05); **pt-5**"` — `pt-5` is a utility-class name used as a CSS property; browsers drop it. Harmless, but it is a utility-class idiom leaking into a hand-written declaration block that also mixes `flex-row`/`gap-20` classes with raw style. (5) **`updateSpectatorHUD` INTERPOLATES WALLETS AND A MATCH ID INTO AN INLINE HANDLER** — `onclick="window.openSpectatorWagerOverlay('${matchID}', '${spectatorMatchState.p1_wallet}', '${spectatorMatchState.p2_wallet}')"` — server-supplied values in a single-quoted JS string inside a double-quoted attribute: the class fixed with `data-*` plus a delegated listener in the surfaces the handler gate flagged. (6) **`handleMaintenanceUI` REACHES `bar` BEFORE ANY NULL CHECK** — `bar.classList.add("hidden")` runs on the `!active` path with no guard, while the rest of the file consistently uses `if (!el) return`. (7) **Honest strengths:** `highlightStartButton` carries the legacy-element fix in place — `const btn = document.getElementById("start-btn"); if (!btn) return; // #start-btn is legacy; the consolidated UI starts matches via window.StartMatch()` — the null guard that stopped the engine's `Cannot set properties of null` panic; **`showToast` lazily creates `#toast-container`** with the reason stated (*"so a toast fired before the static #toast-container is in the DOM (e.g. early WASM boot / dynamic import) never crashes"*); **`updateSpectatorHUD` computes a named, documented synergy formula** (*"Base (100) + Buffs (15/ea) + Mood Alignments (25/ea)"*) and **destroys its own HUD when spectating stops** (*"PILLAR 5: DOM Integrity"*); **`handleMaintenanceUI` has a real interval-dedup guard** (*"Prevent restarting the interval if the target hasn't changed"*) plus a priority class ladder; `updateEnforcementHUD` renders three independent badges from three **engine-state expiries** rather than flags; the null-guard discipline is otherwise consistent (`adjustMapZoom`, `updateMissionHUD`, `updateMapStatusIndicators`, `syncBoardParticles`); and `shareTournamentVictory` builds a real share URL rather than a toast.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the presentation layer and the two cross-cutting contracts) — **the file that states the overlay close rule more clearly than the mandate does**, with a consistent null-guard discipline and three recorded dead-name fixes at its tail; its defects are **`showToast`'s two competing fade timers** (which is why a `critical` duration reaches only one of them), **a particle/SFX ladder keyed on substring-matching server text** whose fallback fires a specific effect, and **an unguarded `bar.classList` access** on `handleMaintenanceUI`'s inactive path.

- **ENTRY POINTS:** ~60 ESM exports, **most marked `// Exported for use in app.js`** — the app binds ~20 as globals while `admin_suite.js` imports the rest directly. Both paths exist deliberately (the suite's table calls the *imported* function, so a control works whether or not a global exists).
- **CALLS OUT:** **`${CONFIG.API_BASE}/api/admin/*`** throughout (`mutation-audit`, `ledger-audit`, `node-health`, `season-rollover`, `force-payout`, `asset-forfeiture`, `maintenance`, `rules`, `ban`, `broadcast`, `network/add`, `network/active`, `reward/*`, `dlc/*`, `power-scaling`, …) — the **correct absolute-origin convention** — plus the WS `nonce_request`.

- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **`renderShopTokenPresets` CARRIES THE `??`-PRECEDENCE CLASS — `if (!cats?.length ?? 0)`.** The negation binds first, so the `?? 0` is dead and the guard's *intent* (`if the category list is empty, say so`) is expressed through two operators whose interaction is not readable at a glance. Same family as the `asset_viewer.js` / `early_tasks.js` / `particles.js` / `world3d.js` findings — here on a guard rather than a string. (2) **THE GATE REQUIRES WALLETCONNECT AND THE SIGNATURE IS READ FROM `sessions[0]`, WHATEVER CHAIN IT BELONGS TO.** `if (walletProvider !== 'walletconnect') { showToast("🚨 SECURITY POLICY: Administrative actions are restricted to WalletConnect sessions only.", "critical", 10000); return null; }` — a deliberate policy, consistent with `signClient.session.getAll()` being the only signature source. **But the chain is chosen AFTERWARDS from the address prefix** (`userAddress.startsWith("0x")` → `personal_sign` on `ETH_CHAIN_ID`, else `algo_signMessage` on `VOI_CHAIN_ID`) while the topic is `sessions[0].topic` — so **a wallet holding several sessions signs against the first, which may belong to another chain**; the wallet rejects it and the failure surfaces as *"Auth Failed"*, not as a chain mismatch. (3) **`cachedAdminHeaders` IS CACHED BY WALLET AND NEVER INVALIDATED** — `if (cachedAdminHeaders && cachedAdminHeaders['X-Admin-Wallet'] === userAddress) return cachedAdminHeaders;` — so one nonce and one signature are reused for every later action in the session, with **no expiry and no logout path**. If the server issues single-use nonces every action after the first fails; if it accepts the reuse the proof is weaker than it looks — and **the client cannot tell which**. (4) **SHOP-TOKEN PRESETS ARE A CLIENT-ONLY STORE THAT NOTHING READS.** `SHOP_TOKEN_KEY = 'nft_seduction_shop_token_presets'` → localStorage → `window.__shopTokenPresets`, while the consumer `resolveShopToken` **returns `'VBV'` unconditionally** with its roadmap branches commented out. The editor renders, saves, re-renders and confirms *"Shop token presets saved."* — and **the saved value changes nothing**; the panel's own hint (*"Lock each shop category to its settlement token"*) describes a capability switched off pending the multi-token milestone. (5) **THE EDITOR PRE-SELECTS FROM THE RESOLVER, SO IT OVERWRITES THE STORED CHOICE** — `const cur = presets[c] || resolveShopToken(c);` renders `VBV` for every row (the resolver ignores the preset), and `saveShopTokenPresetsFromEditor` then re-saves that same `VBV` over whatever was stored. **A preference is silently replaced by the editor displaying it.** (6) **THE MODAL USES TWO INLINE HANDLERS** — `onclick="…remove()"` and `onclick="saveShopTokenPresetsFromEditor()"` — the second being one of the **eight previously-dead admin names** now published by `admin_suite.js`. (7) **Alert-throttle state is module-level and never reset** (`let lastPlatformAlertTotal = 0; let lastGhostAlertTotal = 0;`), so a reconnect within the same page keeps the previous totals and can suppress the first alert after a re-sync.
- **REPAIRS THIS FILE CARRIES (each with its reason in place):** `adminAddNetwork` is the **real** implementation that replaced the stub which toasted success without reading a field; `splitUrlList` (comma/newline/semicolon) lets **several indexer bases be registered for failover**; `fillAdminNetworkForm` lets an entry be **edited rather than clobbered**; `toMicro` converts reward input **by digit arithmetic**; `updateAdminRewardRegistry` renders the **served** registry; and `getAdminHeaders` returns `null` on every refusal path, so no caller can send a partially-signed admin request.

Deliberately does NOT auto-route to any feature overlay — the dashboard must land on its own Tier-1 category grid."* — plus two lifecycle calls whose cost is stated: `SlideTheming.resume('dashboard')` (*"wake the dashboard slideshow now that it is in the layout (its cycle skips every tick while the overlay is hidden, so it costs nothing behind another panel)"*) and `paintTreeArt()`. (5) **`openWorldDashboardToTab` HAS NO `cat:` NORMALISATION WHILE ITS SIBLING DOES** — `openWorldDashboardToCategory` strips a `^cat:` prefix (`String(catId).replace(/^cat:/, '')`) while `openWorldDashboardToTab` passes `tab` straight to `switchWDTab` — so a caller holding a stored value in the `cat:` form (exactly what the star store writes) depends on `switchWDTab` to strip it. Two entry points, two contracts, one implicit. (6) **The IIFE is `'use strict'` and self-guarding** — it ends with `if (document.getElementById('world-dashboard-overlay')) init();` — so it composes safely at import and materialises its overlay lazily.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of navigation and the taxonomy) — **the Single-Navigation Mandate's single surface**: a two-tier contract stated in the header, `WD_ROUTES` as the one routing owner, a deeply-frozen `WD_TAXONOMY` published to replace three competing lists, six capability rescues whose reasons are recorded at the entry, and the auto-route defect fixed in place — **its one live defect is `loadWorldContent`'s `api('/api/world-content')`, the double-prefix 404 class in the very file the sweep cited as the correct example.**

### `Public/js/portfolio.js` — 2857 lines — THE READ-ONLY ANALYTICS SURFACE
- **PURPOSE:** the longest header block in the client, and it is a **contract document**: *"portfolio.js — PORTFOLIO: the player's read-only ANALYTICS surface. Renamed from player_profile.js (2026-09-14). The surface is not a 'profile' form — it is an ANALYTICS view of every aspect of a player's standing."* · **OWNERSHIP / NAVIGATION** — *"Reached ONLY from the World Dashboard (`WD_ROUTES.portfolio -> openPortfolio`).
