It never transacts. No purchase, activation, claim or mutation control may live here. The always-visible `.pp-readonly-note` in the hub chrome states this on every tab."* · **STRUCTURE** — TIER 1 categories / TIER 2 screens, *"CONTAINMENT: fixed full-viewport shell. The PAGE never scrolls; only the inner panel (.pp-panel) scrolls."* · **DATA SOURCES** — every route listed **with its response shape**, ~16 primary plus ~22 association/asset sources **marked "every one verified REGISTERED + live 200"** · **THE PRESENT:false RULE** — *"…which is NOT the same as 'no associations'"* · **ASSOCIATIONS MANDATE** — *"Nothing is inferred: where an association is not exported, the screen says so explicitly instead of stating a guess as fact."* · **ECONOMIC INTEGRITY** — *"Money is carried as uint64 micro-units and converted to a display string ONLY at the presentation boundary (fmtVBV). No float is produced for, or stored on, a ledger value. Bar widths are view-only geometry derived from integer counts."*
- **OWNS:** the 19-category / ~54-screen taxonomy · the TTL cache (`state.cache`, `DEFAULT_TTL = 15000` — *"ms — mirrors the wallet-default rate-limit window"*) · **`getJSON`/`getWalletJSON`** · the honesty helpers `sameWallet`, `pickArray`, `hasMember`, `noEngineRecord`, `countWhere` · `fmtVBV` · `renderToken` (the render-generation guard) · the hub chrome carrying `.pp-readonly-note`.
- **ENTRY POINTS:** `window.openPortfolio`/`closePortfolio`, `ppOpenCategory`, `ppOpenSub`, `ppSwitchRegion`, the **deprecated aliases** (*"`openPlayerProfile` is retained ONLY as a deprecated alias so already-cached callers cannot break; it is not a second UI and creates no duplicate navigation path"*), an Escape-to-close listener, and `window.onCareerTierDemoted` (*"surface a career-tier demotion as a toast, and drop cached analytics so the next screen read reflects the new state"*).
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** **none material — this is the sweep's model for mandate compliance, and every rule is implemented rather than asserted.** Named evidence: (1) **THE READ-ONLY MANDATE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A PROMISE** — the notice lives in the **hub chrome**, not a panel: *"🔒 Read-only analytics — all actions live in the World Dashboard."* — placed there after the per-panel approach was rejected *because* the hub defaults to `territories ▸ overview`, so a panel-scoped notice would be invisible on most tabs and for every new player. (2) **THE RATE-LIMIT RULE IS THE FULL FORM OF §3's HONESTY CLAUSE** — *"The server rate-limits wallet-scoped reads (the `wallet-default` bucket refills one token per second). A multi-screen sweep can trip it, and **reporting 'no data' when the truth is 'not read yet' would be a false statement — so retry exactly once, then flag the panel.**"* — implemented as `state.rateLimited = true` plus one 450 ms retry, rendered as an explicit notice and cleared afterwards. (3) **THE HONESTY HELPERS ARE A VOCABULARY, EACH WITH ONE JOB** — `sameWallet` (case-insensitive wallet compare, the repository's recurring defect, stated once), `pickArray(json, key)` (reads a served list under its key **or** tolerates a bare array), `hasMember(map, wallet)` (map-key membership that resolves spelling), `countWhere`, **`noEngineRecord()`** (the `present:false` renderer, used at five sites), and `fmtVBV` (the **single** micro→display boundary). **No screen invents a field**: unexported state renders through `noEngineRecord()` and unknown-shape payloads through `objectArrayTable(payload, …)` (*"every field reported for each pet"*), so a screen cannot silently omit what the server sent. (4) **THE TTL IS SIZED TO THE LIMITER** — `DEFAULT_TTL = 15000` with the reason recorded (*"so switching tabs does not re-hammer the rate limiter"*): a rare case of a client cache whose interval is justified by the server's actual policy rather than chosen. (5) **`renderToken` PREVENTS A LATE READ PAINTING INTO A PANEL THE USER HAS LEFT** — an incrementing generation compared before `setPanel`, i.e. the async-render race handled explicitly rather than by luck. (6) **`getWalletJSON` RETURNS `null`, NOT A BROKEN REQUEST, WHEN NO WALLET IS CONNECTED** — *"so renderers can show a connect prompt instead of an error"* — the no-wallet case is a first-class state, not a failure. (7) **THE DATA-SOURCES BLOCK IS A CONTRACT INVENTORY** — each route with its shape, each association source labelled with its mandate section (§26.4 companions, §25.6.1 ladder, §23 bonded registry, §25.7, §30, §32), and the two routes whose empty shape is stated (`[Loan] (empty -> [] where there are none)`) — which is why an earlier pass could identify the three endpoints with no owner at all.
- **VERDICT:** owner (of the read-only analytics surface) — **the sweep's most complete implementation of `.clinerules/app-entry-mandate.md` §3, and the file where the honesty rules are code rather than prose**: the notice in the hub chrome, the one-retry-then-flag rate-limit rule with the false-statement reason recorded, a helper vocabulary (`sameWallet`/`pickArray`/`hasMember`/`noEngineRecord`) that makes inference unnecessary, one micro→display boundary (`fmtVBV`), a TTL chosen from the server's own limiter, and a render token that stops a late read painting a panel the user has left.

### `tools/server/verify_entry_probe.js` — 1634 lines — THE ENTRY PROBE (the tools row that replaced "read the source and hope")
- **PURPOSE:** *"verify_entry_probe.js — TEMPORARY verification probe for the Single-Entry refactor. Confirms: (1) zero console/page errors, (2) modules previously loaded as classic `<script src="js/*">` tags actually EVALUATED via app.js imports, (3) the corrupted index.html tail no longer leaks JS as visible page text, (4) index.html contains no first-party script tags other than app.js."* — **the word *temporary* is now false in the useful direction**: at 1634 lines and ~240 assertions it IS the client tier's acceptance suite.
- **OWNS:** `resolveChrome()` (five candidate paths incl. `CHROME_BIN` and Edge), `httpGet`/`waitFor`, and a **hand-written CDP client** (`class CDP` — `open`/`on`/`send` over Node's global `WebSocket`, no dependency). It drives headless Chrome with `--remote-debugging-port=9444` in a fresh `mkdtemp` profile and **always cleans up in `finally`** (`ws.close()`, `proc.kill()`, `fs.rmSync(profile, {recursive:true, force:true})`).
- **HOW IT MEASURES:** navigate → **poll for engine readiness, never sleep** — *"WAIT FOR THE ENGINE, not for a guess. The slow part of boot is the WASM engine, and every assertion below assumes it finished — a fixed sleep is both slower than necessary and unreliable on a cold cache. Poll readiness up to `--wait <ms>` (default 20000) instead."* — the readiness expression is `typeof window.GetGameState === 'function' && !!document.body.classList.contains('ready')`, i.e. **both halves of the boot contract**. Then ONE large `Runtime.evaluate` returns a single object and ~240 `check(name, ok, detail)` calls assert against it.
- **THE VERDICT IS FAIL-CLOSED:** `let pass = 0, fail = 0;` per assertion with `console.log('  PASS/FAIL  <name>  (<detail>)')`, then `console.log('[PROBE] ${pass} passed, ${fail} failed'); process.exitCode = fail ? 1 : 0;` — **and a throw in the driver sets `exitCode = 1` too**, so a crashed probe cannot read as a pass. Two honest exceptions at the top: *"No browser found — skipped."* exits 0 (a machine without a browser cannot run this tier) and a readiness timeout prints **`WARNING`** then continues, so the assertions fail on their own evidence rather than on the warning.
- **KEY ASSERTIONS AND THEIR INTENT (documented at each site):** the refactor's own four claims (`no_leaked_js_text_in_body`, `first_party_script_tags_empty`, `zero_console_or_page_errors`, `BountyTracker` restored, `WasmWalletBridge`/`UnifiedAlertSystem` defined, `body_ready_class`); **the vocabulary contract** (`vocab.client_fails_closed_on_a_bad_purpose`); **the career taxonomy** (*"which are the CONTRACT and must fail loudly if they drift"*) with `career.upgrade_is_unlocked_not_forced` and the staff request that *"ASKS and cannot grant"*; the `bonded.*` family incl. `bonded.market_refuses_a_client_named_price`; the `sandbox.*` family incl. `sandbox.derivative_status_claims_no_pass_fact` (*"A resting-state census cannot know a per-pass fact, so the payload must not claim one"*) and `sandbox.light_renditions_are_real_art`; `wd.tier1_renders_categories`, `wd.tier1_hides_leaf_features` (*"zero leaf buttons even EXIST at Tier 1"*), `wd.stars_on_categories_only`; **the placement pass** — *"a root that exists but computes to none would be the same silent failure the fix removed"* → `console.five_operations_consoles_are_dead_no_more` requires `published && root && computed === 'flex' && panels > 0` for all five; and **session (g)'s criminality family** — `criminality.hub_opens_with_every_section`, `criminality.courthouse_control_matches_the_wanted_level` (*"a CONSISTENCY one, so it holds either way"*), `criminality.cyber_intercept_is_reachable_and_its_action_published` (*"an unpublished handler is the dead-control class this probe exists to catch"*).
- **OBSERVED DEFECTS:** (1) **THE RATE-LIMIT ARTEFACT IS THE PROBE'S ONE KNOWN FALSE-FAILURE, AND IT IS HANDLED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.** Nine comment sites record it — *"A 429 here is a limiter reading, not a product failure: retry with a real wait"*, *"A rate-limited read is RETRIED once, never counted as a pass"*, *"we must not pretend the clear failed."* **The rule is right and the residual is documented:** `Problems.md` §26 E records that two LATE assertions (`bonded.card_view_clears`, `sandbox.slide_wears_your_own_asset`) can still fail on a DRAINED `wallet-default` bucket because the later blocks spend the same budget the earlier ones used — proved by the committed probe failing identically under those conditions and passing on a rested one. **An assertion that can fail for an environmental reason is the cost of driving the real app; the mitigation is inconsistent across blocks rather than uniform.** (2) **1634 LINES, ~240 ASSERTIONS, AND NO `--selftest`** — unlike the four `verify:*` gates, each of which proves its detector can report a failure, this one has **no negative control**: nothing demonstrates a broken app would produce a FAIL. Its assertions are mostly `=== true` against values read from the live page, which is sound, but **a read that returns `undefined` (a renamed global, an evaluate that lost scope) fails for exactly the reason a real defect would** — and the file records that trap itself at 1470: *"a SyntaxError that kills the ENTIRE eval (and the failure looks like a missing return)."* (3) **ONE GIANT `Runtime.evaluate` IS DELIBERATE AND ITS HAZARD IS NAMED** — the probe builds a single expression returning everything because *"splitting these across Runtime.evaluate calls loses the closure scope (and the fetch log)"* (the same reason recorded in `verify_portfolio_associations.js`); the trade is that **one syntax error anywhere in ~1400 embedded lines kills every assertion at once**, mitigated only by convention (`node --check` before running it). (4) **`--disable-gpu` MAKES SOME READINGS HEADLESS-ONLY** — the probe distinguishes a limiter reading from a product failure, but the headless flags mean **WASM-exit and compositor accounting can differ from a real browser**, a fact the repository records in its own notes (*"the headless `--disable-gpu` WASM-exit artifact is a separate target, not a regression"*). (5) **THE PROBE IS BOTH THE ACCEPTANCE SUITE AND THE REFACTOR'S RECORD** — its comments carry the measurements the session notes cite (`marked=22 painted=22 missing=0`, `declared=24 inlineHandlers=0`, `hub=true sections=[…]`), which is why the detail text is often as long as the assertion.
- **VERDICT:** **the client tier's acceptance suite** — a dependency-free CDP driver that polls the engine instead of sleeping, runs ONE scoped evaluate, and exits non-zero on any assertion or any driver error; ~240 checks whose comments carry the mandate section, the measurement and the failure being caught, organised by the session that added them (entry · vocabulary · career · bonded · sandbox · WD tiers · placement · criminality). Its honest limits: **the documented 429 artefact on late blocks**, **no negative control of its own**, and **one embedded expression whose syntax error would kill every assertion at once**.

The 26 modules `verify:api` fixed used a helper that already prepends `/api`, so their `/api/api/…` was a genuine 404; this file's prefix is the origin only.
